text: I've been here a few times, and they are often busy but once your order is in, the chefs are fast! Sometimes the service is slow, and I've noticed multiple times that they seemed understaffed which is why it may have taken a while to seat us. Though the food here is pretty good! I've had better around New Orleans, but this place always seems a little more convenient, and when delivered through post-mates it maintains its quality! I love the green tea boba drink here, it's not too sweet like a lot of places. I also always get the lemongrass chicken vermicelli, with light noodles and extra veggies. One time I got it with "very light noodles, extra extra veggies" and they even added some carrots, broccoli and onions, which aren't normally included in the vermicelli dish, but were surprisingly tasty! Overall it always satisfies my craving for noodles and boba tea, and it's in a lovely location, so I'll continue to come here!

Food was very tasty! I had a not so good experience with the lady manager of this location! She was constantly nagging the employee making my bowl even without knowing the order details! Food is definitely delicious and worth trying!

Tried a few Thai restaurants since moving to Brandon, Florida many years ago and this place is by far the best! The décor is really nice and the staff is very friendly. I usually get take-out and have never been disappointed. Give it a try!

One thing that comes to mind after entering the place. Clean! It does not smell like an Indian restaurant like Sitar, Karma or Samosa. The place has a seating for only 12-15 and the place is perfect for a quick in and out buffet. I would recommend this place only if the group is small and do not care about the ambiance as much as the taste of the food. The menu is very limited for the buffet. The price is per pound of food you take. If you are super hungry, 1.5 pounds of food will be perfect for you. Bread is extra. Overall - great food, hole in the wall.

The best Thai restaurant I've gone to in a very long time! Reasonably priced! Large portions! Very clean! Bartender was welcoming which made my experience greater! I enjoyed the medium red curry and shrimp tempura! Umami was a very pleasant experience!

Baguette deli is a small place located on the side of a Fred Meyer in Boise. They offer Ban Mi sandwiches, Pho, and a few other items. The Ban Mi and the Pho are the reason to be here. The crusty bread, very fresh, crunchy vegetables, and delicious meats, along with a $5.00ish price tag make this place a winner in my book. They also offer bowls of Pho, which again are delicious, and very reasonably priced. There is not a lot of sitting room here, and it can be a little messy (tables not always cleaned quickly), but it is still worth it. If you are lucky, they will have some beignet's . They go fast, so look for them on the counter display. MMMMM. If you're looking for a healthy, delicious lunch, go here.

I'm Trinidadian therefore, I love Caribbean food and absolutely loved this place, everything was delicious. The family that owns it couldn't have been any kinder and accommodating. We'll definitely be back!
Awesome Cuban and Mexican food and amazing Mojitos. Try the Lime in the Coconut drink. Great service.

Called up and was greeted by a very nice woman, Helped me to decide what dish I wanted. Perfectly seasoned, spicy wonderful green curry with chicken. Vegetables were perfectly cooked, spices were balanced wonderfully with this sweetish basil coconut and spicy green chilies. What a treat. The perfect ending to a long hard day. I will definitely be back to try the other curries.. I ordered for take out and seriously considered going down to hug the chef this was so good.. Thank You!!

First time here. Heard from a friend that it was great and it was!!! Ordered the special of the day, Clay Pot Tomato Beef with bean curd. Excellent. Very tasty. Also got the Walnut Shrimp. Incredible. Large perfectly breaded and fried shrimp in a rich, creamy sauce with crisp, candied walnuts. Our friends both had the Wor Won Ton soup which they enjoyed. Huge bowls filled with bbq pork, shrimp, won tons, vegetables and noodles. Will definitely be back!!!
Excellent spicy chicken noodles. Not quite as good as authentic hand pulled but overall superb flavours.

Since the departure of Pho Tau Bay I've been at a lost for a good Pho and Báhn Mi. Lily's surely delivers on both. Last time I stopped by was during a very busy dinner service to try their vegan spicy tofu Bánh Mi which was rated as one of the top 15 in the city. It was delicious! Vegetables and bun were fresh and tofu delivered on the heat. The Phos are also very good and nice size and I swear that kitchen works at warp speed. Good for lunch, dinner dates or large gatherings.
crab and mushroom omelet need i say more!!! oh yes, bloody mary Atmosphere was great. Staff delightful. Highly recommend

The roti was great. The coconut bun was great. The provision with saltifsh was a little imbalanced, but in part that's my fault for getting provision when I know that's not my favorite dish. I feel confident enough that the roti and coconut bun are representative that I'm comfortable giving five stars.

Came with a friend for the lunch buffet. The service was fine and we were seated promptly. There was a pitcher of water on the table, which I appreciate as a serious drinker! The vegetable korma and garlic naan were very good, everything else was standard fare for an Indian buffet. Also there was a mango dessert dish that was new to me, and delicious! I love Indian, the location is convenient to the Indiana Convention Center, and I would go back if in Indianapolis.

I stopped in for lunch here while shopping with my Mom on Magazine Street. And the staff was lovely and attentive. The space is really open and attractive. The food was good and the prices were inexpensive compared to other Vietnamese places. And the food is more traditional than some of the other spots uptown/garden district. I had veggie avocado spring rolls and they were perfect. My Mom had a small pho (which was huge for her) and she really enjoyed it. I also had the bun with tofu and it was OK. There were definitely regulars who must be in all the time since they were greeted and asked if they wanted their usual dishes, which I would appreciate if I were a regular. The porch seating seemed to be dog friendly too. The steps were a bit steep and my Mom did struggle with them a little but she had been walking all over the place for a few hours.
wonderful food, great service, and a lovely location! food was a bit more expensive than we anticipated, but incredible quality!

My boyfriend and I came from out of town and had fantastic service and a fantastic meal. We checked out restaurants in the area on Yelp and thought this would fit the best. Thankfully our instincts were right. My boyfriend got the salmon oriental and I got the rack of lamb (lamb out of New Zealand). Normally I am not a fan on salmon, but the salmon oriental had amazing flavors (the sauce was awesome). The rack of lamb was cooked to perfection and tasted fantastic. We also had a great server with good suggestions. She helped us make good decisions and answered all of our questions. From start to finish, we loved our experience. The bread and oil before dinner, drinks, the house salad with the ginger balsamic vinaigrette and our meals had us very pleased. Add a great waitress and we were in heaven! Please go if you make your way to St. Petersburg!

This is absolutely my favorite place. I had been to the one in Scottsdale and nearly died when I found out they opened in Tucson. Where to start. The restaurant itself is beautiful. Each meal starts with a basket of hot flat bread and a plate of herbs and butter. If you look to the corner of the main dining area you can see the bread oven where the flatbread is made all evening. There are so many good choices and our server Jessica helped us pick some great dishes. Service was excellent and the food is just amazing. I had the chicken Shish with zereskh polo...if you've never had any Persian rice dishes, they are all worth trying. This one is basmati rice with saffron and barberries. Barberries have a hint of sweet and a tang that might be something like a sour cherry and dried cranberry taste. Every time I eat here I wonder if the food is really as good as I remember and it always is even better. Also...the portions are quite generous so come hungry, be excited to take food home, or in my case, also place a massive to-go order for all the sad people you left at home.
The gyro is fantastic! Kabob (chicken) looked great, but brother in law would let me try!

I (like others) am hoping that this place is just in their "getting our feet wet" stage. I REALLY hope this place gets better. I enjoyed the potato Dosa. Prior to cooking it, they asked my spice level liking which I said was a 3-5. Well, their definition of 3-5 is much higher than mine (in other words my Dosa was SUPER spicy. Great but almost TOO spicy). I will adjust accordinlgy next time. I hope they learn to keep more options available later in the night in the future. Alot of the food seemed to be gone at about 8:00pm and they stated that what they had was what they had (in other words they were not cooking any thing additional to choose from). I ordered a few curries and apps (basically I took one of everything they had left). mothing stood out except the Dosa.

Our inaugural post comes from the Warehouse District's newest restaurant: Compère Lapin. Top Chef fan favorite, Nina Compton, like many of us, fell in love with New Orleans and couldn't bear to leave. We are grateful. Compère Lapin's light but decadent Caribbean fare is perfect for Nola's summer foodie. Atmosphere: With a hipster-Portland-like vibe, the classic bar, eclectic light fixtures, and art collection adorning the walls, gave us plenty of visual stimulation. (Edith especially loved the conveyer belt fans.) Needless to say, you'll feel a little bit cooler just for having dined here. Food: Any place that serves chive biscuits with bacon butter is fine by us. All of Chef Compton's dishes had a near perfect balance of textures and flavors. The rich, smoked tuna tartare and avocado was balanced with crispy plantain chips and fresh mint. Though the curried goat was melt-in-your-mouth-tender, the oyster roll, a playful twist on an oyster poboy, stole the show. A soft, buttered brioche-like bun cradled crispy oysters topped with a sweet and spicy pineapple slaw so light that it nearly tricked us into forgetting that we were eating fried seafood on bread. We rounded out the meal with a shockingly refreshing coconut tres leches cake. Service: The service was friendly, efficient, and attentive. Our server offered us extra biscuits when our second course took an extra five minutes AND brought the check promptly because he knew my husband needed to return to work. The staff smiled at Edith, remarking how cute she is. (This is clearly worth extra points.) Feedith Rating: Yay! #feedithnola Highchairs: Yes. Changing Table: No. Sufficient White Noise (i.e. can't hear my kid scream): Yes! Parking: Easy street parking + affordable lot directly across the street

One of the better Indian places in the city. Food looks and tastes fresh. Easy on the stomach and on the pocket. The number of dishes may be less, but whatever is on the menu is cooked nicely. Nothing is overly done with cream or spices. Perfectly cooked. Today was my first time here, and I am definitely going to frequent this place. Also, Mumbai Bistro is located on the intersection of DELHI street and Locust st. (between 9th and10th), which is kind of ironic :)
Absolutely amazing! Must get the black garlic wings - they are to die for! My brisket ramen was delicious as well, I can not wait to come back!
Stopped by after Christmas shopping, grabbed crab fried rice and chicken drunken noodles. The wife and I love id, so glad the deliver ;). Will have to order lunch sooner than later! Thank you

Cool place! Cute little wine bar in a retro filling station in a residential neighborhood near the Botanical Garden. The waitress was very knowledgeable about wines and the manager came over and introduced himself and talked to us for awhile. I went with two other friends and we also ordered some light food. I had a Turkish pizza which was incredible. Nice relaxing atmosphere. We sat inside as it was a little muggy, but the outdoor patio was open where they were showing some silent black and white movie. We also took a tour of the basement where the wine cellar and a private tasting room are. And if you go up the stairs, there is a restaurant, which I believe is in a former apartment, Elaia, which may be a future trip. I will return to Olio and also want to check out the pastry shop across the street, Choquette, which was closed that night. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because it's small and kind of cramped, and I can imagine if we had gone there at a busy time, there would have been nowhere to sit.

I went to fez with a friend got humus and a Side of rice, the worst rice I have ever tasted , it tasted like a microwaved 3 or 4 day old rice. Asked our server to remove it and he informed us he couldn't, okay and when we preceded to get the bill he had given Himself a hefty 8 dollar tip, okay? Never coming here again.

Quite simply, this food truck is amazeballs. Yes, this is a Thai Mexican fusion truck. An undeniable awesome marriage between two of my most favorite cuisines. I swung by to try their famous Cap'n Crunch crusted tilapia burrito but I ended up ordering their entire menu. And I wasn't even hungry! THAI SHORT RIBS TACOS (1 for $3)- Tender yet perfectly chewy. The flavors literally burst in your mouth letting you know these meats were given a good marinade bath before it was cooked. Generous slices of avocado canopying the filling of veggies like shredded cabbage and cubed tomatoes. And oh my, that green sauce.....creamy, yet light and refreshing. CHICKEN KATSU W/ AN EGG ($5.50) Extremely crispy, thin flat cutlet of well-cooked chicken served with a bed of slaw, a fried egg, rice, and spicy mayo drizzle. Ask for extra sauces! CAP'N CRUNCH CRUSTED TILAPIA TACOS (2 for $6)- The disadvantage of coming here late to avoid the long lines was that they ran out of burritos' ingredients. However, they accommodated us by making us a taco instead! Made with the same love as the ribs tacos, except with the crunchy, slightly sweet breading, and delicious flaky fish inside! I don't generally expect good service from a food truck. But the people who work here go above and beyond with their genuine helpfulness and friendliness. I was super impressed with my entire experience. I only spent $15 for all of that deliciousness and I was 100% satisfied.

Would have loved to try it! We walked in at 8:15, they close at 9. We were waiting on friends and were confused about the locations, so asked an employee about it, who told us there were multiple locations, and added 'you better decide soon because we close at 9.' That could have been 5 paying customers who ordered Pho. Shrug.

LOOOOOOOOVE this place! The ambiance is nice, the food is great, and the staff is friendly. Everything on the menu is delicious, but my favorite way to end my meal is with the churros and chocolate! Definitely the best part. I would recommend this place a thousand times over for a good breakfast meet up with friends.

Really mixed...fundamentally I don't think it my kind of food - the seasonings, the sauces, etc. We took my adult daughter protesting. Her husband and I were more open to it. Wednesday night quiet at the restaurant and no one watching front of the house and seating people. Finally seated on patio which is nice. Ordered nachos. the kids ate them but said they weren't what they expected. Their steak wrap and black bean burger were delivered but they weren't excited by them. My seared tuna with fruit and Vinaigrette were outstanding. I never would have paired the tuna with fruit. But that being said, one out of three happy customers isn't enough so we won't be returning.

This became one of our default go-to places as soon as we tried it. There are some dishes that we love so much (starting with the Tom Kai Gai Coconut Soup for her and the Tom Yum Lemongrass Soup for me) that we get them every time. Beyond that we've loved everything we've tried but tend to over order just because there are so many things that tempt us.

I love Dominican food and was excited to discover this affordable Dominican restaurant on 12th and Callowhill. Friendly staff made for a good start but the lack of air conditioning made for a stifling and uncomfortable meal. There were a variety of dishes to choose from. I had the tres gulpes and was underwhelmed. The fried cheese and salami were good but the base of the meal was mushy and not flavorful. My friend had the Tilapia which came out black. I did;t ask her how it tasted but it looked severely If I were to go back again I would order the chicken lunch special - half a chicken with rice and beans for $7.50. Also getting it to go would prevent from having to eat in an un-airconditioned room. This place has potential unfortunately I didn't feel like it was quite met.
Basically all I can say is it's delicious. From the mango lassi to the food. All around yum.
The hookah flavors tasted great and lasted for a long time. The service was kind of shitty at times but everything worked out. I had a great time here.

Good food, terrible service. I was running errands and stopped by for a quick bite by myself. I sat at a 2 top next to the window and then moved over to a 4 top because the table was in direct sun and really warm. The entire restaurant was 25% full at best with 6-8 vacant tables and the owner came and told me I couldn't sit there because it was just me. Rude. Moving on, my spring rolls were awesome and my stir fried chicken bowl was ok, a little too much gravy on the chicken. I waited a good 10-15 minutes after I was done for the server and owner to notice I was still waiting for a box. I asked for the check and she never returned. I finally waited in line at the counter and paid . For what should have been a very quick lunch turned into more waiting than anything else on what was not a busy time. Perhaps take out is a better option here.

How to even begin to describe the let total let down that was lunch today. First, had to call back 3 times before we could place order, they just didn't seem to have any of the favorites. Fine, so finally it became a conversation about "well, what do you have?" Please note, it's not like we called at 2:28 for lunch, it was a reasonable 11:45 or so. Second, delivery was ridiculously late, maybe being from NYC I have higher expectations so I'll give them a pass on that...maybe. Third and the final straw, the food was HORRIBLE!!!!! I don't even understand how they felt that what they sent out was acceptable. How does a Dominican restaurant screw the most basic thing-Rice. It was stale and crunchy...and not in a bibimbap way....which I love but not with my chicken stew that was void of everything but chicken. The only redeeming item were the sweet plantains and I assume that was because it didn't require much intervention from the chef. Was this just an unusually bad day for a restaurant that thus far has been pretty good? I don't know but it will be quite a while before I return to find out.

All I can say is WOW! I made a reservation last minute for 25 people and Priya made it happen! I came from Atlanta to Philly and she literally took care of us like family. She had the table ready and even got graduation balloons for the graduate. They took our huge cake and stored it for us and also put candles on it! She brought out the most amazing appetizers and the food was phenomenal. We got paneer tikka masala, paneer lacha, methi mataar spinach, Kashmiri lamb, chicken tikka masala. Their chili cheese garlic naan is to die for! We brought our own beer and her servers stored it AND brought more out for people as needed. I've never felt at home more than 16 hours away than as I did that night. We left them lots of yummy cake and we cannot wait to go back again if we are ever in the area. Thank you Priya!

Good food, good service, fair prices. Just what a guy likes! They are about a block off Main Street, but hey if you prefer to pay for over priced food, stay on Main Street! They also have a good vegetarian selection with ethnic flavors. What else can I say ... give them a try!
Great food and service!! Thank you for the great time and stopping by to check on things Mohammed! Try ANYTHING!!

This place now called Thai Smiles is a gem. It is a regular place for us to eat now. And we are never disappointed . Food is fresh, atmosphere is great, very clean and always fresh flowers on the tables. Check it out. We are fortunate to have such a fantastic place un our back yard. I always get the garlic and pepper checken. Awesome!! :-) :-)

Was hoping for more of an Israeli touch and menu but still good and a close feeling to home cooking by my parents and my friends parents. Would go back for sure when in the area and walking by. Good coffee

This was my second visit to Zac's. First one was fine, the ​second one not so much. Walked​ in on Sunday around noon, waited in line for 10 minutes to be seated, must have been 5-6 empty tables dirty, no one was clearing them off. ​The whole time we were in line, food was stacking up to be served under the lamps. I would say at least 10 plates, meanwhile,​ then waitress​ were chatting​ in the corner​ while the food grew cold. We continued​ to wait for a ​booth, meanwhile,​ people behind us were leaving saying the service was better at McDonald's​​, they were on there way there. We were finally shown a booth and the waitress​ never came over, still in the corner chatting with more food being piled up. Zac's has really gone downhill with service. Also,​ the ladies room was out of service. At that point wasting​ a half an​ hour to be seated we left, as well as other customers. Mj

Love! Love! Love Sis. Muhammad's Kitchen! The food is excellent and I am always very satisfied with any meal that I get. My favorite is the fish hoagie. The hoagie is super big and enough for 2 people to share. This spot is very popular so sometimes the wait is long, but it is always well worth the wait. My advice to people is order your food in advance of your hungry point. If you order when you're hungry then you may have an issue.... LOL! Great food! Keep up the good work. Im definitely a fan:)

I can't believe that I haven't yet written a review for this place. I've been coming here since they opened this place and immediately loved it! Here is where I was introduced to the Panang Curry. Definitely one of the best in town. Also they have a dish called Mee Kati that I have never seen at any other restaurant. I tried that as well and it is a great dish. It's a sweet dish so I prefer to add spice to it. I have never had Thai home cooking but I feel as if this is what it would be like. It's family that works here and from what I was told they eat what they make because it is what they would do at home so that says a lot to me. Their Thai tea is excellent but I think their iced coffee is even better. The staff is always great and it is a very strong reason why I keep coming back. They keep the place tidied up as well. No doubt a place to check out if you're in the area, and if you're not, make your way out here.

This is an absolute MUST visit. Everything about this place is damn near phenomenal. The food is fresh and clean; you can tell it hasn't been frozen or sitting in a fridge. The service is great! All of the employee's there are friendly and helpful (I can barely pronounce "perform" correctly). They have a lot of Gluten-free and Vegetarian options, which is nice.

I was so excited to see another Greek restaurant in Carrollwood Center...right where the previous Greek restaurant had been. I ordered a chopped Greek salad to go with chicken breast. It was over $10. When I got home with my meal there was no chicken...and no potato salad. And even worse, there was barely any feta cheese to be found. All other toppings were in abundance, but without the potato salad, chicken (which I paid extra for), and very little feta cheese, I was very disappointed. However they did give me enough dressing for three salads! On a positive note, the place was clean and the service was very fast.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Loved eggplant curry . And great costumer service . I Will definitely like to go again.

I love Mediterranean food, but among standard fare, even the best rarely surprises. This is where Suraya stands out. Even staples like babaganoush and hummus are elevated here, offering nuanced layers of flavor incomparable to what I've found elsewhere. I'll be dreaming of this spot as I try to reverse engineer these items from home. Also: the cruller is as good as they say -- don't miss it.

Slow service, food was just OK. Had the beef and shrimp with vermacelli and lemon chicken. Only two shrimp the size of my pinky. Lemon chicken and beef were a step above Panda Express. 30+ minute wait for food.

I love this food truck. They have the tastiest street foods like their captain crunch tilapia burrito. Who would've thought of that? The fried fish is so flakey and delicious, paired with fresh cabbage, tomatoes, avocado and Sriracha mayo. I have also tried their katsu and curry chicken which are so rich in flavor. Their Thai tea is also on point! So much to offer from a small food truck. I live in Jersey and I have driven here many times just to get food. They are so friendly and provide great food at a great price.

This place is fantastic! Top notch, couldn't find a thing to complain about if I tried. We sat in the back yard/ garden. It was like stepping into a Mediterranean/ middle eastern garden. We were actually supposed to head in for dinner but just couldn't leave the beauty of that garden. Drinks: extremely unique. We tried "the poet" but there were a bunch of awesome craft cocktails plus a full bar. Food: delicious! You don't get access to the full menu in the yard but the stuff that we did have access to was amazing. Service: excellent bar, waiter and support/ management. Really made us feel at home. * note: we went without our kids. Changing tables and children friendly bathrooms were not assessed! We'll see if there a deal breaker here....

5 Star AUTHENTIC Jamaican food. Tougher location but the Jamaican vibes are worth a visit. We had them cater our wedding rehearsal dinner. All of the guests (most have never had jerk) were very impressed with the meal! Jerk pork, jerk chicken, rice & peas, beef patties, DG brand drinks; they have it all. We drive an hour and a half to stop at the walk up window just to enjoy the food. Orda di jerk grab a DG and enjoy di vibes, every ting is Irie!

Traditional style Japanese restaurant that's my fav in the bay area. Love that you can sit on tatami mats or tables. Waiters/waitresses wear kimonos and their green tea is excellent :) My fav appetizer is the Agedashidofu!!!! I coudl order it 10million times and never get sick of it. mMmm! Sushi is the best around and prices arne't terribly bad. Salmon teriyaki is really good too. I love JotoS!
The soup I had was very delicious. My girlfriend who is a vegetarian loved this place because they had a lot of options for her. If I was in town, I would go back.

I have been to mostly all of the Caribbean restaurants in Philly and I have to say that Ron's is the best! Yesterday I visited for the first time and fell in love. There were about 5 people in line when I arrived and my order was taken within minutes. There were 3 people taking orders and the line moved very quickly. I loved the fact that they kept the food coming out. As I stood there, a new pan of mac and cheese and yams came out fresh and hot, not like some restaurants where they run out of food or make you wait forever for food to be made. The jerk chicken was well seasoned and moist, the oxtail was good, the mac and cheese was REAL mac and cheese and was delicious. The plantain was sweet, moist, perfectly ripe and the best I've had in the city so far. Candied yams are my favorite food so I am very picky and I must say that I was pleasantly surprised with the yams as well....fresh, sweet, real yams (not the canned stuff some restaurants give you). Ron's I will definitely be back even though I have to travel about 40 minutes to get there. Worth the trip! 5 stars!
Most of the food I've had here is pretty good, sometimes dishes are a bit bland, but overall a pretty good vietnamese spot.
A++ for food quality, selection, ambiance, service, and price. This is the best Thai on the Gulf Coast.
Delicious food and the staff was excellent. Couldn't have asked for a better date night. Oh, you have to try the Thai Tea. DamnGood!!
Came here from out of town. The service was great! Gave 3 of us Free drinks. Clean and yummy!

Place is legit AF. Owners very nice. Fast service. Price is very reasonable considering it's all you can eat. Food is delicious. They rotate the desserts to mix it up, but always have 3 to choose from. Tea is included. 2 different kinds of rice, salad, appetizers, soup, etc. all included. My favorite Indian buffet by far.

I ordered the grilled beef with veggies and rice. It wasn't the best meal I've had (I wouldn't order it again), but the other stuff my friends got was really good! The spring rolls are really tasty too, I recommend getting them as an appetizer. Overall, a pretty good experience. Clean restaurant setup and good food!

My fav Vietnamese deli in Pinellas. Excellent Bahn MI (tofu of course) and chicken vermicelli. Awesome selection of Boba tea (ginger is my favorite but the avocado-coconut is also wonderful ). Only minor complaint is the spotty WiFi (works maybe once of every five visits) and could use a better Pho selection, but the food they do have is great and service is good.

We stopped by Kanella for breakfast and it was definitely one of my highlights on our recent trip to Philly. As soon as I read the breakfast menu online, I was salivating. We started with the dips of the day, which were traditional hummus, a potato garlic dip and a pumpkin feta dip. They were all great, but the pumpkin feta was out of this world good. The wife and I were trying to figure out the ingredients so that we could replicate it at home. For my main breakfast dish, I went with the homemade lamb merguez sausage and duck egg, which also included some spicy cured pepperoni and spicy yogurt. The wife chose the cumin scented tomato and pepper stew with poached eggs and grilled bread. Both plates were beautiful and delicious. For dessert (yes, we made room), we got the fillo pastry filled with semolina custard and the coconut/date/hazelnut cake. The perfect end to the perfect breakfast. Our server was great and very knowledgeable about the menu. I look forward to returning for dinner next time.
I travel the world and eat at a lot of places and this place has the best Indian food I've ever had!

It's hard to find a decent cheesesteak around u-city. Well I just found one. By far one of the best cheesesteaks I've had around here. Better then Abners!! Worked in u-city for almost 3 years and see this truck everyday, never even crossed my mind to stop. Came here based solely on yelp reviews. So grateful that I did. I got a cheesesteak with hot peppers and their special bui sauce which is some kinda like spicy mayo. And it hit the spot. Definitely will go back...maybe even tomorrow!!

This hole in the wall family run Korean bbq place is worth checking out. Their variety of pickled and fermented food is truly mind boggling, and their kimchi represents the Korean classic quite well. there are so many sides that they have to transport them to your table via a cart. They have tabletop grills and will let you take control and cook your own food. The bulgolgi was very good. I'd caution against the pork belly on grounds that it's pretty boring. The bi bim bop (perhaps the funnest named food ever) was only decent; I just wanted more flavor.

Wait was a little longer for the food, but came out super fresh so I am ok with the wait! The Greek salad was delicious!! My boyfriend got the gyro and it was delicious! Their fries are super fresh and tasty.

The food is delicious and well presented. We had a party of 10 for dinner and the staff stayed on top of all our orders and requests. Ambiance is nice, easy access plenty of parking. Definitely worth the drive. We will be going again and soon!

Tandoor did not live up to expectations. The food was bland and oily. I highly question the palettes of people that are giving this place anything higher than 2 stars. My roommate and I had take out from this place a little while ago. We both agreed that the food was mediocre at best. The next day, we were both sick from it. They did throw in free desert, which was nice. Perhaps they do this to win over customers who otherwise would not be satisfied. I'm never going back again.

Not sure why I hadn't tried Ruby Cafe before but had some friends visiting from out of town and decided to give it a shot for lunch and was impressed. Honestly we didn't even look at the menu but instead just ordered the buffet, it was $10.95 and had a nice selection of items. They had 3 different types of rice (Regular Basmati, Dill Rice, and Sweet/Sour Rice), 2 different types of lentil's, Chicken Stew, Eggplant Stew, Chicken and Ground Beef Kabob, Stewed Spinach, Hummus, and a large variety of salad items including Feta Cheese, to top it off they even had dessert items of Baklava and Lemon Cake. The food was very fresh and flavorful, the rice was cooked perfect and the salad items were fresh, not to mention the Chicken Kabob was one of the best I've had in Tampa. There was only a small amount of people dining at the restaurant but the food on the buffet was fresh and quickly refilled when out. The service was also good and the ambiance was comfortable and the waitstaff was attentive. I could eat there every day!

Overall great experience. Food was delicious and the portions were very large for the price. Service was good. I had no complaints. The firecracker chicken and brown rice and honey walnut shrimp were all great.

First time at the new location on South St, but worth the extra half-mile hike. I agree that this place can be slow and no one's gonna accuse the wait staff of being too attentive, but they serve a good meal. I recommend the Sansom kabob, sort of a mixed grill of grilled lamb, grilled chicken, and the star of the show: the Chablee kabob (ground beef mixed with onions, garlic and spices formed into a long kabob -- delicious!) -- comes with grilled onion and tomato which are very good compliments, as well as brown rice with a nice topping that's sorta like a thick hummus (plus afghan bread and a little salad). Went on a Wednesday evening and there was barely anyone in there, so I got my food quickly. My sambosa appetizer (not quite as good as an Indian samosa, but still good) arrived in just a few minutes. I always leave sated and happy and feeling like I had a refreshing and balanced meal -- it's not cheap (Sansom kabob is $18 for dinner), but well worth it!

We came here for a work luncheon. Since we were busy discussing work, life, and everything under the sun, our waiter/host was very patient with us. He checked on us a few times and when we sent him away again, he told us to just flag him and let us know when we were ready to order. He was so polite and accommodating! One of our party ordered the lunch special of lamb kebob, another the chicken kebob lunch special, and I ordered the Mantoo. We each tasted all the plates that came to the table, and let me tell you something: it was all delicious. The lunch kebob plates were reasonably priced (under 10.00) and the Mantoo was out of this world. My husband also had lentil soup (which he said was fantastic) and an amazing Persian tea. On the menu, Mantoo is described as ground beef and onion raviolis topped with a special yogurt and lentil sauce. The presentation is beautiful and the ravioli filling is savory, fatty goodness. You can taste the fat in the meat, and the yogurt and lentil sauces on top compliment it and cut the richness of it so that it doesn't get overwhelming. I do wish that the Mantoo came with something like rice or a salad, because all you get is the raviolis, but next time I know to order a side. We finished by sharing a baklava and Shir-Berenj (rice pudding). My friend asked us to take the baklava away from her because she was afraid she would inhale the entire thing. The rice pudding was less wet than others I've tasted, and I liked that. If you want to save a little, go for the tasty lunch specials. However, if you want to go all out, ask to sit at one of the low tables decorated with Persian rugs and hookahs, and order as many yummy dishes as you can! This would make a great spot for a special dinner with a sizeable group.
Very sweet service. Home style cooking. Delicious food. Authentic experience with care. enjoyed a lovely experience.

AMAZING. EAT HERE, NOW! We saw this place on yelp and decided to give it a try. Fantastic experience. Friendly, prompt service. The food was perfect. Imaginative, well spiced, generous portions and all around excellent flavor. We will definitely come here again!

This is my favorite Moroccan spot in Philadelphia. It's clean and very nice. Sometimes parking can be difficult but never too bad. The staff is friend and man men. Not man speak complete English but they can understand you. This place is excellent for groups and just couples. My recent visit was with my boyfriend. We had the Fez feast. It's $30 pp and comes with a few dishes which is fulfilling but I would've love to have more chicken and a half chicken could feed one person especially if both don't eat all meats served. We had the lemon chicken and I was so delicious, full of flavor. The lamb was tender and good. I enjoyed this other dish which had chicken and scrambled eggs inside a warm dough with sugar. The mint tea is good and was included. This is a good spot to relax mingle and smoke hookah. I would recommend to anyone who wants to try something different. Since I've been to Morocco I would say this is very authentic!! Go, have fun and enjoy yourself!! No drama just a good time!! Food is goo! Excellent service.
Hummus deluxe was awesome. Ask for more bread though. Roasted cauliflower is an underrated sleeper. It was fantastic. It is served warm, but can cool quickly on the bread. Eat quickly!

Even though I don't live anywhere near Mood Cafe, I regularly travel across the city for their chaat and lassis. The owner is sweet, funny and generous--I have seen him send an indecisive pregnant woman home with an extra chaat on the house, just in case she second-guessed her choice of flavor, and today when I asked him to explain a certain seasoning to me, he gave me a free second drink so that I could sample it. The food is always wildly flavorful and so, so satisfying, whether as a summer picnic meal or a light, spicy way to warm up in wintertime. If you have any questions or want a recommendation as to what to order, be sure to ask the owner! Hearing his explanations and having him customize your chaat and lassi is an important part of the Mood Cafe experience.

My wife and I have been here multiple times now. We've had a great experience every single time. The boba teas are awesome and the sandwiches are huge. The Pad Thai is also very good. The staff is always very friendly and the customer base leads me to believe that it's a very authentic place.
Each time I come I get the same thing.... A kabob with chicken and sausage. Just get it. Slide it off of the stick and mix it all together. You'll love it trust me.
The people here are very friendly, pleasant and polite. Food always very hot and good quality. Fast and efficient service too.

We were tourists that escaped deep-fried-shtuff (DPS) of French Quarter in search of something plain and comforting. We found this place based on the yelp reviews, and I feel obliged to say thank you for all the reviewers and the restaurant owners and staff. Clearest broth, option to add veggies to it (do it!), crispy sprouts, and when you can't wait for it a variety of spring rolls you can have... This was by far one of two most satisfying meals of my almost week long trip to New Orleans.

fantastic food, don't let the mundane look of the mini strip mall bother you. Once inside a quaint & contemporary décor awaits and the food is very tasty . Lunch combos are small but they happily made me a little extra . Don't skip the Lamb Rogan Josh and the Goat Curry.

Food was delicious. Been awhile since ive had good indian food. Had chicken tikka masala, vegetable biryani, vegetable samosa and garlic naan. All was great and made with care. Definately a place ill be returning too again and again. The rice was very good. Good job

Great environment and very friendly bartenders / wait staff. The food leaves a little to be desired, though. We had just eaten at Sang Kee a few days before, and by comparison all the food we ordered at Shanghai Station just didn't make the cut.
Wonderful find off the beaten track! A terrific take on the southern meat and three where local food and Southeast Asian flavors blend for a fabulous, well-priced meal. The banh mi was delicious!

The family and I enjoyed our dinner at Pan d'Olive very much. I called a few hours early to make reservations, however it was probably not necessary since the place was 3/4 empty when we got out there at 7:30. The ambiance was great though, and the servers attentive and willing to accomodate our food modification requests. We are not picky eaters by any means but it is always nice when restaurants go out of their way to ensure that even the slightest customer's desires are fulfilled! They serve a basket of sliced bread and olive oil and cheese as a starter. We ordered 2 appetizers: hummus and calamari. Entrees were flatbread napoleotana, veal marsala and lobster ravioli. As dessert we had the baklava, new to us but we enjoyed it very much. Everything was super delectable, however my favorite thing was the hummus and pita bread. I don't know what magic ingredients they put in that hummus but it was astonishing!! Um um um. The happy hour at Pan d'Olive sounds pretty amazing, so I will be checking that out soon!
Everything was really good. Fresh veggies. The scallop cakes tasted more like whole scallops than some mix of seafood & filler!

Great cappuccino and other espresso based drinks. Plus good salads, hummus and snack-y foods. Free wifi and comfy, homey seating. Cute barristas (male & female) and well poured shots of eeeeeeeeeee. Comfortable homey environment. Beats the hell outta fourbucks. I'm a fan!
I only had their lunch buffet. The food is excellent and the spices will make your pallets dance bravo to the chef and I can't wait to try their dinner menu.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Went there for lunch buffet and found it be only a few items. Very limited selections. Food is good though but wished there was more. Give 3 stars for limited items.
Eat at the bar so you can have Kristie wait on you and have her make you one of the best martinis ever. The rigatoni is super light with leeks and amazing meatballs. Wonderful service.

I was worried moving to SB I wouldn't find a decent Thai restaurant but while we were up for a day visit looking for apartments came across the Mesa and this little Thai place and we've loved it ever since. The service can be shady sometimes, they're kinda all over the place and forgetful but whatever. The food is consistent and I'm a creature of habit to always order the same Thai dishes at different restaurants (its easier for me to gage whether or not I like the place). Its just too bad they don't deliver. I have yet to find a decent Chinese restaurant in SB but still searching...any suggestions?

First time trying Ethiopian cuisine so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I loved the experience of eating with the injera (bread) from a family-style platter. I'm a meat lover but the veggie sambussa appetizer (lentils with spices and veggies in a flatbread crust) was awesome. My friends and I ordered the queen's eight dinner: chef's choice of 4 veggie and 4 beef/chicken samplers. Can request all veggie and mild vs. spicy. It's $15/person and the cooks prepare each platter based on how many people are sharing. Ours included the gomen with beef, tibs wot (beef in a stew with veggies), doro wot (chicken with hard boiled egg), ye kik alecha (yellow split peas), ye misr wat (red lentils), atkilt alecha (carrots, potatoes, string beans), and a couple of other yummy dishes. Though the platter didn't look like a ton of food, it was extremely flavorful and filling and we had quite a heavy take-out container of leftovers. Traditionally they don't use utensils but instead the injera, and the restaurant does offer silverware if you prefer. They also serve beer and wine; the Ethiopian amber was delicious. Docked a star as the server knew we weren't familiar with the restaurant or Ethiopian food in general but didn't bother to explain what any of the items on the platter was when he brought it out. Just placed it on the table and left. We later asked and another server helped us. There were only 3 other tables of patrons by the time we finished but they took over 25 minutes to get our check, and even by then were confused on what exactly was ordered/owed. Unique dining experience. Overall the staff was nice and the food was amazing. Kudos to the kitchen.

THIS PLACE IS AMAZING! It's right near a friend's apartment, so we walked over without a reservation and were seated right away. I'm a vegetarian, so I assumed I would have to starve through the lamb and chicken courses, but my friend told the staff and I was brought a separate dish for the meat courses! So wonderful!! I LOVED the eggplant appetizer and the lentil dish, it had amazing root vegetables in the middle. Baklava dessert was TO DIE FOR. The belly dancer was great and the other patrons were all having a great time, which made for a really wonderful dining experience. Will definitely go back the next time I visit philly!!!
Probably my favorite restaurant in North Country! Food is terrific , drinks are good, great music, and the owners are very nice and accommodating. I go at least twice a week.

Truly a hidden gem. Fantastic, charming service, nice cozy atmosphere with unique and delicious home cooked food. Lots of vegetarian dishes, but we went in another direction. We started with an Ashak appetizer, an incredible lightly steamed dumpling covered with a meat, yogurt sauce. Also tried The Bulani appetizer. It was a crunchy fried potato and onion pastry with a yogurt dip. It's a BYOB, so we brought a decent bottle of champagne and saved a lot on the bill. I ordered the Qablee Palaw which was tender marinated lamb with almonds, raisins, carrots, and rice. My wife had the lamb kabob, grilled, smoky and very tender. We finished the meal with afghan style ice cream, and baklava with two strong coffees. Perhaps the best and most affordable meal we've had in town in the last several years.
First experience with Ethiopian food. Yummers. Super nice people here. And the coffee....wow...it will bring me back.
Great vibe! Cool gastro lounge on beach drive! Great people watching spot inside or out! Dog friendly and super music! Wednesday night is 1/2 off appetizers - just bring a lady!

I was visiting Media from Philly and was looking for a quaint little spot for dinner, from the outside this place looks great. It was Friday evening and there were some open tables, so we were seated quickly. Service was not bad, although it took a while for someone to come to our table and food took a long time as well. Lots of take outs, so we figured it was good food so worth the while. Unfortunately, the Pad Thai and Massaman curry were a big disappointment, and I say this because I am a big of fan and get these dishes regularly. Overall, not impressed with quality of food. Other than that, it's a fine place for casual gatherings. Maybe there are other dishes that are better, we only had two!

I like Remedy. Haven't tried too much of the food, but have had the wraps and am waiting to still try the dosas. Given that I my roots are from the south of India, I must say that I tend to have very high expectations for the dosa clan of food items which is quite different from North Indian food (naans etc.) Now, what I have tried I really ilke. They make an awesome Himalayan chai which is green in color. Strongly infused with crushed pistachios, extremely flavorful and filling. It's caffeine free too. It's really more like flavored milk. I also like some of the other things out there. They have a large variety of tea bags that you can pick up for your hot tea. Remedy has some seriously filling muffins etc. to go with tea/coffee for those just looking for the cafe experience. Mostly whole grain muffins with high fiber and filling as hell, it's great for an afternoon break from work kind of thing. I like 'em. The food looks very good, to be honest. I can't wait to try some of the things. Dosa is one, but even some of the more traditional north indian varieties look pretty good. Another review will appear, once I've tried the food!

This place is a regular for me. Everything I've had here is fresh and delicious. Surprisingly the sushi was great as well. The pad se ew is the absolute best. It's not on the menu but the still make it. It's delicious. The Thai fried rice is great as well. Great, relaxing atmosphere and great food!

Delicious! Three of us got the jerk wings appetizer, the lamb shank (with couscous, stewed tomatoes and onions, and cabbage/carrots for sides) and the jerk ribs (red beans and rice, and seasoned fries for sides). Everything was deliciously seasoned, the meats were fall of the bone tender, and the sides went together with the meals perfectly. Huge portions for the price. Staff was very nice and the manager checked in on us. Definitely worth a visit! (Forgot to take pictures, but trust me it was great!)

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: They are back! This is my family's favorite place to go out. Birthdays, milestones, post-traumatic stress recovery - all are celebrated at the Taj. We were at a cultural loss as to where to go for the last year. There are some new items on the menu - chicken achar is an excellent new entry. Achar is tangy and is a nice complement to the creamy korma. palak subzi dal is a spinach dish with other veggies. The spinach was a little over cooked, and maybe from frozen spinach (yuk) but this might be the way the dish is normally prepared. I can't wait to go back and sample the channa and okra. There is also a beef tandori which sounds great. They have a lunch buffet which would be a good time to sample a lot of the staples. We also enjoyed the garlic naan which they dialed down a little for us. Nick, I think they have always had the extensive drinks menu. They have switched to a lot of regional brews. I'm a fan of the Rogue products. The nutbrown ale was nicely malty and combined well with the savory achar. At the old incarnation of the Taj, I experienced my first ever Tripel Karmaliet. It is really amazing to pair the sugars in beer with spicy food. The new space is cozier and probably more affordable to maintain. I hope this family business thrives so that I can grow old with it.

This is probably the nastiest food I have had in a long time ! ( my opinion ) . The mac and cheese had a weird sage like flavor with meat ( perhaps sausage or chicken) and onions . That might sound good but it wasn't good at all. Also ordered coleslaw (it was the lesser of the evils) and pasta salad with pesto ( it had a weird flavor ) . But The worst of all was the overly greasy undercooked chicken wings . The chicken literally reminded me of undercooked "shake and bake". The wings were pink inside and inedible . They charged a la cart for the sides and sauces . Those little cups were 3 bucks and the sauces were nasty too ! I called the Resturant to complain and I was given a managers number more hassle . Listen - don't waste your money . This didn't taste like it could be redeemed. Waste of money !

This place is definitely worth trying once, and it's especially fun with a large group. The food is average/decent, but there is a cute appeal to the unique presentation. Also, it's easy for communal bonding to ensue when everyone's eating with their hands and sharing family portion dishes. A bit of advice: during the first course, hoard up on pita slices when the server passes around the pita basket. While most of us politely fished out a couple wedges of pita and passed the basket on, the wise one who'd eaten at Marrakesh before stowed away an impressive amount of pitas in his towel. Ten minutes later, he came to our rescue when the rest of us all ran out of pitas while being far from finishing the platter of great eggplant dip/veggie platter. The pita basket only gets passed around once, so remember to stock up!

We really enjoyed our meal here. I came in w Husband and 2 littles and they were gracious and accommodating (prepped steamed veggies and a sauce just for kids on request). Decor is beautiful and peaceful. Many different level options for sitting. Food was great - husband had the giant steak with an unusual sauce and I had a pho (which I was graciously taught how to pronounce when I asked). Kiddos had the fresh spring rolls and ended up drinking the peanut sauce. Well priced wine list with a good portion- and I can't wait to come back for a lychee martini. Thanks Liam we'll be back!

Wow! This place is dirty and has the worst service ever! I really wanted to give this place 1 star but the food isn't bad. Service -0. no greeting, when the server came up to take my order he just stares at you awkwardly without a word. Hmmm okay, guess I should order now. When they got us our food they just left it and took off without a word, no checking up on tables with extra napkins, water or tea. They also forgot our tea we had to remind them. No courtesy, no smiling, and of course no apology. Food 2- I was hungry so it didn't taste too bad but it was not great either. Atmosphere -0 dirty and I heard other customers were complaining that they found something in their bowl so the server took back that bowl to the kitchen. I didn't hear anyone apologizing or offering anything for the customer. And I found a strand of hair in my bowl as well. The sad thing was I was almost done with my food. I didn't want to bring it up to the server because it wouldn't make any difference and they probably wouldn't do anything about it based on what I saw.

I hadn't had Indian food before going here, and I found out about this place from my brother-in-law's wife who went to the University of Arizona. I'll admit I was a little apprehensive going in the first time, but it was really good every time we went back and we make sure to stop in whenever we're in Tucson. Tonight, we were craving Indian food and wanted to get out of the Phoenix area for a while. This was the obvious choice. My wife had her usual chicken tikka masala and mango lasse. I had the shrimp masala. We also shared the keema samosas appetizer, made better by the tamarind sauce, some kashmiri rice with some naan. The masala wasn't as spicy as I was expecting when I ordered it at a medium spice, but I'd rather have it be not hot enough than too hot. The masala mixed with the kashmiri rice piled on the naan is like an explosion of flavor that I can't get enough of. The atmosphere isn't too Americanized, nor is it cheesy over-the-top Indian - it's just right. The music that they pipe in isn't too loud, and it's really enjoyable. The service is always quick and friendly. The restaurant itself is smaller, but instead of feeling like a sardine in a tin can, it feels cozy. This is one of the few places my wife and I are willing to drive 2 hours just to have dinner at. If you've never had Indian food and haven't wanted to try it because you've heard it's really spicy, give this place a try (they'll make it as spicy as you like it, even if it's not spicy at all like my wife likes it). You'll be in for a nice surprise.

Absolutely fantastic experience from the moment that you walk in you are taken care of. When we mentioned that we were having an anniversary there was more attention to our special occasion. Every part of the meal was excellent, with much appreciation and acknowledgement of every staff member to make sure that our experience was out of this world and at the end the chef complimented us wit h banana liquor and zeppoli. And we got a nice gelato with a little sparkler on it to commend our 9th anniversary meal. As far as the food is concerned wow is all I can say just wow I cannot express the way that the food was such an experience. Highly recommended!!!

Finally a Banh Mi place in Wilmington. Yummy sandwiches, fresh and flavorful. Lots of bubble tea options. The owner and staff were really friendly and cute little sitting area to eat. Was going to take a pic of my Banh Mi but ate it too fast, was dying to try it. Will be a regular spot!

I was excited about their grand opening. The cashier was really nice and the place looked great. But they didn't give us our ice for our desserts, and we were missing a drink. It was a bad first impression for me.

Pikpon is a small, clean and spicy little shop you could easily miss because the sign is too small. Thankfully, Yelp finds even the most hidden gems. I ordered the Spicy Basil Fried Rice (peppers, onion, string beans, chili & egg) with chicken, which is enough for 2 people. The dish is medium spicy, but plenty hot for the average palate. Chicken was plentiful in the take out dish. I will definitely return for the Lobster or Pad Thai, or one of the many Thai drinks on the menu.

Probably the only reason I am giving this place 3 stars is because I didn't have pho. I decided to grab the house friend rice, and it was lackluster, small portion, big price and no flavor. The pho my girlfriend was having seemed to be good and a great size portion! Service was good, and friendly staff.
"Great food and great service. Prices are very reasonable and food is always fresh. Ask them for the spice tray to kick it up a notch."

I had to stop and review this spot! The individuals who serve us at this place are very kind, and their food is always amazing! Most recently, I had the jerk chicken, dark, with rice and peas. Portions are nice, and it was Sooooo Bomb! I don't live in Indy anymore, and I make it a point to eat here when I visit. 55555 stars!!!!!

Had Thai Ice Tea it was very very sweet. could drink even quater of thr drink. Ordered Penang curry and Yellow curry, they serve it with rice which server in the same dish as rice. Both curries were good.

I usually come here to get the banh mi. I believe it is the best in the world. I had my share of banh mi from California, Texas, and Atlanta. Always get it extra spicy with sriracha aoili. The bread is from Hi-do bakery! Today I came in for my usual banh mi, but Chef P told me to try his Phoritto. I heard about this in California but never tried it. He insist I add an egg to it also. I was a little iffy at first. Pho and EGG wrap like Wth right. All I got to say is BRAH! BRAH! It was not dry, yet it was not soupy like pho. The pho broth infused noodles reminds you of an actual bowl of Pho. The balance of Hoison to sriracha was on point, but the kick of the lime and cilantro sealed the deal. The banh mi is my favorite, but the Phoritto is not far behind.
I was in the mood for beef. The tenderness and flavor of the meat was excellent. Service was great too. In a city of great food you always have so many choices. I would choose this restaurant again.

I just spent 6 months living in Thailand so when I got back to Nashville I was desperate for a good, authentic thai place. After trying nearly every thai restaurant in town I feel confident saying that this is the best thai restaurant in town. And the staff is so friendly, I go here now just to keep my Thai sharp. Definitely go here if you like Thai food because if you haven't been here you haven't really had it.
Fez feast is the best. Go for the lamb and the lemon chicken. Great hookah, fun atmosphere and good times.

I really want to like this restaurant - I really, really do. I've ate here many times, however I get really mad sometimes because they screw up my order or give me rice instead of fried noodles. I don't think I've ever gotten my chow mien the right order. This is a family run chinese fast food place, it's really cheap and they give great discounts on bulk orders. It's great for fast family dining and lots of other options. I don't have an issue with the taste, or portion sizes. I honestly really want to like this restaurant, but they've screwed up my order 3 times in a row. Not kidding! I even ask to not skip the noodles but they give me rice instead, I ask why? and they say "it's what we have" despite the description says fried noodles. I would give this place 4 stars if I didn't have issues with my ordering. Tampa doesn't really have many options for Asian food, maybe Pei Wei down the street. Overall if you want decent chinese food, Top China is good.

Food the was great. I just wish they would turn on the AC. It is always warm/hot in the restaurant. They have all the fans going but I feel any cool air. It's pretty bad when the outside feels cooler than the inside of the restaurant in the middle of summer. Would have given a 4 star but needed to rate the food as well as the environment. If your so hot and uncomfortable, it's hard to enjoy your food.

Nice little quiet place hidden in the Bucktown area. Service is fast, plenty of seating, a lot of parking available. The food is pretty tasty, and portions are generous. However, you will get less hummus during dine in then when ordering to go.

I have been to this restaurant several times when I am in town. Sometimes, I will make my way from LA or San Diego just to stop by the beach and Thai food. I'm Thai and it's hard to find a good Thai restaurant to my standard. The quality of food is higher than many Thai restaurants I've been to. My favorite dish is Seafood Spicy fried Noodle! I enjoy New Zealand Mussels, shrimps and they throw crab claws in this dish. It's fancy and delicious! Staff always work so hard to get customers in and out quickly. Friday and Saturday are always packed. The service is fast and excellent. I highly recommend Siam Elephant and it always is my favorite Thai restaurant.

The enthusiastic reviews of my fellow yelpers made me choose this small and brightly colored restaurant as my lunch destination yesterday. The small menu looks interesting, the people behind the counter could not have been nicer. We started with the Harira Soup - bland and thickened in a way that reminded me of soups out of a can. Even though my companion and I were hungry at the beginning of the meal, this soup made us wait for the plates we ordered, the Shawarma Chicken and Lamb Ketban. The chicken was incredibly dry and tasted like cardboard, the lamb (pieces of leg), while cooked freshly, tough and innocuous. The only think we really liked was Zaalouk (sauteed grilled eggplant in garlic and tomatoes with olive oil). It was beautifully spiced and very tasty. When I looked at the Tagine dishes patrons at the next table ate, I regretted that I had not ordered chicken or lamb tagine. They looked so much better than the brittle pieces of chicken on our plate. Because of this and and the wonderful people behind the counter, I give Marrakesh Express three stars instead of two. One more thing: When a place is opening at 11:30 a.m., why is the special of the day not ready at 1:00 p.m.? Even the Moroccan tea was not ready until 1:30! This is not a good way to run a restaurant.
love the catfish, cheap, grilled fish, cheap,good service!!!!!!

8th & Union is by far the best restaurant in Wilmington, DE. Service is superb. Highly recommend the buffalo cauliflower, calamari. All the burgers are amazing, cooked to perfection and to order. The Gouda burger is to die for.

This is a bit of a step up for the restaurant. But still not much. I had a seamless gift card, which I had to use before a certain date. So, the only restaurant near to me which delivers is, Desi village. I ordered the Malai Kofta, Bhel Puri, Garlic naan and Aaloo paratha. Malai Kofta was decent but the sauce was a day old. And there was no aaloo (Potato) in aaloo paratha. For Bhel Puri they had all the ingredients seperate, which is good. But again, this will be the last place I will be looking for to have dinner or lunch.

My wife and I have traveled throughout the Middle East and enjoyed food along the way. This local Brandon restaurant's food is authentic as it gets. We ordered the mixed grill and mixed salad that my wife and I shared. Both were excellent choices and there was plenty food for both of us to share. The food was bursting with flavor! We talked to the couple that own the restaurant and found out the husband only wanted to use their current location to open a catering business. His wife convinced him to open the doors so they could operate a restaurant/takeaway business too. Lucky for us she did. The food was very delicious. I would have given a 5 star but the restaurant appears to be in the middle of renovation.
The avocado citrus and steamed seafood were amazing and the cooks prepared the food in front of us. Definitely go on a week night when it is less crowded!

When my fiancée said he found chef Nina's restaurant in NOLA and there was goat curry on the menu, we knew we would have to plan to dine there, so I between the Hermes and the Bacchus parades, we were able to walk over for a late 10pm dinner. As we walked to our table, we saw chef Nina in the open kitchen, and if we had had time for a drink, we probably would have grabbed one at the bar and watched her in action. But instead, we sat down at our table in the back of the restaurant and perused the menu. Drink of choice when in NOLA is the sazerac, and theirs was very good. The kitchen sent out some biscuits with 2 butters (chives and bacon) they were gone pretty quickly. For starters, I ordered a half a dozen oysters, and we shared the conch croquette and spicy pig ears to share. The croquettes were perfect and balanced out the saltiness of the pig ears. For mains, we ordered the Caribbean seafood pepper pot and the goat curry with the black eyed peas and roasted potatoes as sides. The pepper pot was too fishy for my fiancée, and the sour notes did not pair as well with the rest of the meal - probably wouldn't order it again. But, the goat curry, OMG!!!, it was melt in your mouth, nestled amidst pillowy sweet potato gnocchi, with a rich sauce, that we just scooped up until there was nothing left. Our evening was made extra special when Larry stopped by our table to check in on us, and we shared with him how we had seen him and chef Nina in Portland, about a year earlier while we waited for our table at BokeRamen. He explained to us what they were finalizing the investment for Compere Lapin, and that they come to Portland fairly regularly. Who knew!?! If you're in NOLA, this is a must on your adventure!
Chicken pho was pretty delicious. Service was really nice. The noodles were good, though I wish I had a little bit more for the size I ordered but it still delicious.

This restaurant is a special gem in Reno. The food is incredible. The owner is lovely. If you are not familiar with Ethiopian food, you should definitely branch out your culinary wings and give it a shot... You will not be disappointed. It's all true!!!

LaVa is conveniently located on the corner of 21st and South, just a few blocks from my place. Over the past few months it has been my go-to for quick and easy lunches when I'm on the run. I'm a big fan of their hummus platter, paninis, and oversized salads. Staff is friendly and attentive, atmosphere is pleasant. The only downside is that it is usually pretty crowded, so if you can't get a table or you're waiting to take out, it's a little awkward standing around.

I enjoyed the chicken with coconut rice, both times I was here. The flavor is great, but the chicken portion is not enough to fill me up, so I had to order an appetizer. I've been here twice and will definitely return. Low Prices, so with the app, I spent $11 plus tip. Also, the food is very spicy if you order anything with hot pepper on it. I love hot and spicy foods, but if you can't handle tobasco, you won't be able to handle their spice, as it is a little hotter than that.

Restaurant.com users beware.... Meal was nothing special. service wasn't good. Was told that they will not honor restaurant.com certificates even though there is no expiration date on the certificate .... just left mine behind and told them I won't be back. Also, a $5 fee for BYOB. Honestly, I don't mind paying for good food but this place isn't good .

There are a lot of cool new restaurants popping up in Nashville and this one stands out at the top. My wife and I used to go out regularly but life with a baby has obviously cut down on that quite a bit. That being said, we tend to put a little more thought into date night. This was one of the best dining experiences we've had in Nashville. The menu is perfect for having a couple courses - very interesting, small starter options - they have a 4 for $16 option - perfect way to try multiple things, but still not fill up. Then for the mains... the Pork Belly Gnocchi was every bit as good as it sounds. Overall - I rarely take the time to review restaurants but really want to give this one the praise it deserves.

Being in the area for St. Vincent Carmel Hospital, this was a quick drive to satisfy my Indian food craving. The Indian Masala Tea was hot and good. The Chicken Curry was delicious and had just the right amount of spice. I upgraded to the Kashmiri Naan to offset the heat and to satisfy my sweet tooth at the end of the meal. A perfect dinner for me!
Serving time was awefully long and food too expensive for portion! Wouldn't recommend

I was trying to find somewhere to get dinner in philly around Christmas on a busy Saturday. But my the grace of god I was able to get a reservation to Spice Finch at 5:45. I've been to a ton of Mediterranean style places in philly - Vernick, Suraya, Zahav, all the best places. I'd have to say that Spice Finch is very competitive with all these restaurants and definitely has better prices. The wait staff was very very friendly and accommodating. Food cake out very fast. Everything was DELICIOUS. We had the cauliflower, clams, carrot hummus, and chicken. The chicken was probably the best I've ever eaten. If I could give this place more than 5 stars I would!

This place is pretty lame if you are used to actual indian food. It costs the same amount of money for a small meal here, as it does for a full, hot, freshly cooked meal at an indian restaurant. The portions are tiny, I was not satisfied with what i was given at all, It lacked flavor, and the amount you get is a joke. I only weigh 130 lbs and it felt like half a meal to me. Its a nice idea, to have an indian restaurant on market street. But honestly this place is a crazy waste of your money, go to india grille, or some other real indian restaurant, there are plenty of options. I will say, if you are in a pinch, the food is absolutely edible, and really not all that bad. Its like some decent food you would find at the airport, with silly high prices for very small portions. But at the airport you would expect that, on market street... not so much.
Great Byob restaurant...grilled roman salad with fig reduction. And chicken parm so big it hangs off the plate. Yummy also open for lunch

Lunch today was the 2nd time i've ventured to this establishment. the 1st time was "okay" but today was very, very pleasing to my palate. everything i ordered was on spot: from the thai iced tea and the spring rolls (vegetarian) to the vegetarian pad thai. my friend was introduced to thai food for the first time (she had a chicken dish w/ sweet & sour sauce) and she's now a fan. the dishes are reasonably priced, our service was mediocre (he forgot that my friend's dish was ordered with chicken), and it's very close to my neighborhood. i'll be coming back numerous times.

Hands down the best falafel in the city. Not only is it amazingly good but you get enough food for almost 2 meals and it's all for just $10.(this price has been stable for some time but it can vary. Safe bet would be to hand him a $20) There's no ordering so you line up, receive your container, and pay but I've never had a bad experience from whatever he decided to dish up for the day. However, be warned, you will smell like char grilled chicken and garlic for the rest of the day. It's a small price to pay for this awesome food. The only negative thing I'll say about this truck is that you should expect to wait. He does not rush his food and if there are 10 people in line a 30+ minute wait is not out of the question. I've timed him at about 3-4 minutes an order.

My boyfriend brought me here for our anniversary and I couldn't have been happier. We shared hot tea and the vegetarian combo plate. Both were amazing. I had never experienced any African food but I definitely see myself coming back to get the coffee ceremony. The service was fast and friendly. Overall this was a great experience and I would recommend everyone to try this place.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I haven't written hardly any yelp reviews, but I had to come back to find this place since I've been thinking about my meal here and primarily the mango lassi. Best thing ever. I need to go back to Boise just to have this again.

Phonomenal!!!!! This is probably the best Pho in the east bank! Best $8 you'll ever spend. The Pho comes with plenty of meat and noodles, along with one of the best broths I've had in quite a while. Third time in two weeks, so glad I discovered it!

My wife and I had our date night let night and decided to try something out that we normally can't with our boy... he doesn't eat anything except popcorn and milk. :) Anyway, We very much enjoyed our night out. The food was so very good. I don't know about all these poor service reviews... maybe they've taken heed to the reviews and changed it up a bit? Our service was fantastic and prompt. I love that this place has made it for so very long. I hope that many will frequent this place. I like that we have a diverse selection of restaurants here in Reno. I had the beef combo so I could try a bunch of stuff, my wife had the veggie combo. Everything was awesome, it was a great experience for sure. I personally have nothing bad to say about this place and we plan on going back again and again.

Went to Cheu Noodle Bar for first time yesterday. Was a decent place. I got the Crispy Sweet Potatoe Rangoon which was excellent! Also had the Miso Ramen which was decent. The area is pretty small and there is no where to stand while you are waiting to be seated.

Fez only even gets stars because the food is delicious but here's the catch- it's probably the worst service you'll ever have. Atmosphere: Awesome. The windows are all blocked out (we had no idea it was torrential downpouring) and there are awesome tapestries all over the walls and ceilings. There is cozy seating and awesome gold tables. Great decor. Three of us went here for a celebration dinner with a groupon. We each decided to do the 7 course vegetarian feast. Everything was very fresh and delicious. I liked the second course best although I had no idea what it was. So an hour or so later once we've gotten through all of them we get the bill. Here's where things go south. The first bill had no gratuity added to it as there were only three of us, not five. Once we gave the waitor the groupon he came back with a $19 tip added AND more tax on there. How does that happen?? We read the fine print on the groupon and menu neither of which allowed this. We approached the waitor about it and he wasn't helpful. One of the more bold people I was with then went to the manager with it and he would not even look her in the eye and said they added gratuity for 'more than two.' Shady business. We even told them we were going to tip them- and in cash not on our cards. If it weren't for the whole tax/gratuity debacle I'd go back in a minute. But, they were so rude about the whole situation that it left a bad taste in my mouth (not to mention my friends as well). So, if you want good Moroccan food and a cool atmosphere and don't mind getting ripped off and having terrible service- go here. Oh- and I didn't get my opentable points even though we filled our reservation. And we got bread that looked like it was from Amoroso's instead of pita? Strange behavior all around...

Atmosphere - Pretty intimate BYOB. They even have an area where you can sit on the floor and eat, though it was empty when we were there. Service - As good as you can ask for. Servers were all kind and patient. Food - Good but not great. It didn't blow me away but definitely very good. Drinks - BYOB Overall - The food is good but the prices seemed pretty extraordinary to me and I've never been adverse to paying for quality food. $23 for a Lamb Kabob plate that wasn't anything special seemed extreme to me. I think you can get the same thing at most places for less than half the price. I might be inclined to try it again since it's about two blocks (maybe less) from where I live but probably not. Points for: Atmosphere. Service. BYOB. No points: A bit pricey for what you get.

Delicious, authentic Indonesian food. We had the kwetiau goreng and lontong sayur. Both were generous portions and brought back memories of Indonesia. Having lived in Medan, Indonesia for 9 months, I was thrilled to discover that the owners are from Medan. Definitely trying the nasi campur Medan next time! I highly recommend this place to anyone who misses Indonesia or just wants some Indonesian food.

Is it the best Indian food that I have eaten? No; probably not in my top three, but the food is pretty good. Living in South Jersey, it is good to find a spot to pick up a meal on the way home that doesn't require me going to a fast food our curb side pick-upchain. Good place to have a nice lunch, buffet is small but plentiful.

I love Mumbai Bistro! I work a few blocks away and their super fast, free delivery is a Godsend on those days I accidentally leave my lunch at home; I will admit that I sometimes accidentally-on-purpose leave my lunch at home these days just so I have an excuse to call the guys at Mumbai. The food is crazy cheap for Indian, even the worst things on the menu are still decently good, and the small portions keep my pigginess in check. The restaurant itself is reminiscent of a generic chain, but I actually think the food is quite good. Others have mentioned the nan and veggie samosas could be improved. I agree (and will add the tandoori chicken to that list), but they're still yummy.
