Their chicken biryani, chicken vindaloo, paneer masala, channa masala, tikka masala, mixed veg curry, and basmati are all delicious. I've probably been in or ordered delivery a dozen times since discovering them about 6 months ago and I have never had a disappointing meal. Contrary to some other reviews, I think the food is aromatic and overall very good - some dishes are lacking in heat, but it's nothing a little hot sauce can't remedy. The place is clean, the service is quick and friendly, the food rocks, it's cheap...what more could I ask for?
This place was very hard to find!!!! Upon entering the campus, there are no signs directing you to the restaurant. Other than this place being hard to find, the food is good!!
Delicious fast/casual gyros and such --- love the salad, the hummus, and the tabouli too! Very small dining area and a bit exposed...but for takeout, Yum,
Best Pad Thai ever! Their Crab Delight is also amazing! I eat at this restaurant so much that when I call they say "Okay Ashley see you in 10 minutes" I love the food and the staff!

I think it's about time that I write a review for this place. I always come here for my boba fix and vietnamese coffee. It's not the best boba that I ever had but it satisfies my boba cravings. I am giving this place a 4/5 because they have decent banh mi (vietnamese sandwich), boba drinks, and vietnamese coffee. +2 stars - good food. The bread they use on their banh mi because its fresh and the outside is crunchy. My favorite is the tofu banh mi because it is just perfect with the egg, tofu, and the awesome bread they have. The grilled chicken is dry so you may want to choose other choices. I also tried their beef pho and I definitely recommend it because the broth doesn't taste like there is too much MSG added to it but it needs more meat in it. +1 star - convenience. I just call ahead for my banh mi or any order and they tell me that it will be ready in 5-15 minutes. I definitely recommend that you call ahead so they can get your order ready. +1 star- good boba drinks. They are not my best so far but their drinks definitely satisfy my cravings. I love their vietnamese coffee because it is strong and it is more coffee than milk which for me means I am getting my money's worth because I am getting more of the coffee. I like my coffee strong so if you prefer more milk then you may have to tell them that you want more milk in your coffee. -1 star - okay service. Overall, they just have like a fast food service where they take your order and give you your order. They were rude to use that one night my family and I were there but possibly it's because they were almost closing so they were tired. LOCATION: it's next to Honeybaked Ham and across the movie theater plaza on US 19 in Pinellas Park. They have a parking lot behind their restaurant as well as in front of the place that is along US 19. Overall, I will still come to this place and try other things on their menu.

I've had Albasha three times in the past few months. Today was my first visit during lunchtime. It's been solid every visit. My favorite is the veggie plate. You get 'a little bit of everything' it seems. Lots of food for a decent price. I will definitely be going back.

Glad We Went Through this Gateway We visited their restaurant on Bay Pines Blvd. It was quite good. We started with the Kerala Shrimp appetizer which needed a little more zip. My wife had the Butter Chicken which was heavy and needed some brightness but was otherwise good. I had the Tandoori Platter which was great. The chicken was very tender and flavorful. We got a side of Tamarind Chutney which was fantastic. It brought the brightness that some of the dishes needed. We also got a nice Mango Lassi which should have been tarter but was nice. The Garlic Naan was terrific. Service was very good and the restaurant is nicely decorated and comfortable. I would definitely return and I would slather that Tamarind Chutney on everything.
Great place for lunch. Also, they have the best strawberry cake I've ever had in my life.
Today was training day, and the food was free! Service was great and the food delicious. Can't wait for this place to open full-time!

Worst service, food and prices possible. I have never written a review before but I just could not let this one go by. I made a reservation here for my birthday. My friends and I arrived there and were kept standing by the door for a half hour. The place seemed full and there was no place for us to be seated. Not sure what the point of making the reservation was...aren't they supposed to hold a table for us??? After repeated requests to seat us we were taken to a dimly lit backroom by a service restroom. Service was slow and the waiter took his time to come and take our orders. We had to ask several times for a performance by the belly dancer before she came and did a cursory performance. The worst part of everything was the food which ranged from completely bland to inedible.I just could not understand the combination of a sweet pie with almonds and chicken with powdered sugar and then lamb with honey on top. Even thinking about the food from last night makes me want to throw up. "Desert" was bananas, apples and oranges in a basket with a knife to cut it ourselves!!!! After sitting through the worst possible service and food, we were stuck with a bill of $520 for 8 people which included an $80 tip!! I would recommend everyone to stay as far away as possible from this place.

reading the reviews makes me wonder if i went to the same place as the other reviewers. i had reserved a table for one for 7.30p this eve. upon arrival, i was seated at the worst table in the house: the one by the entrance, in which the two seat options were either immediately behind the entry door, which would hit me each time it swung open, or on the opposite side of the table where the vent was blowing ferociously on me. i chose the latter as long as the waitress offered me the next open table. a deal was made, and thankfully carried out right after the bread was served. one waitress seemed to be catering to every table so it did take me a few minutes to receive my turn, a rundown of the menu, and the obligatory introductory bread. i opted for four pasta dishes, explaining to her to leave out the seafood in any of them due to my allergy. each came out quickly in succession, as per request, but the main carbonara dish came with the swordfish, rather than without, so i left much of it untouched. the rigatoni and gnocchi plates were solid; the pesto pasta was rich on basil, which was not to my liking, but not the fault of the restaurant. my waitress noticed the carbonara mishap and offered to bring me a new one, but i was ready for dessert. i ordered the almond panna cotta, which was this evening's highlight, easily. light yet filling and with fruit to complement the airiness. i was offered a complimentary zeppoli dish of doughnuts over nutella and did finish those, which also did please the palate. my three stars are for the table situation, the quick and almost abrupt nature of the waitress in serving me (no niceties or time to mingle/linger), and the cold, cold dining room. seriously: bring a parka. the food was overall presented well, through i will likely never head to nj (from philly) for dinner again as it's a far visit for a culinary scene that cannot compare to philly's.
Great service great food very inviting staff and the atmosphere was fun. Stop in and try their pho or vermicelli, some of the most colorful fresh Vietnamese food I've had in a while!!
Just ok. Nothing special going on here except the service which is excellent! Food I'd mediocre at best

Came in and the guy just looked at me like I was lost. wasn't phased so I asked him if I could sit anywhere. Took a seat and my partner and I got a menu. So far okay :) Asked for the drinks he had and he pointed at the fridge. Umm okay... So I got up and looked at the fridge and picked out a drink. He looked as confused as I did. Well anyway we got our order and the food was okay. I've been to a lot of Pho restaurants in town and I can safely label it a 3 star place to eat. Today I had the flame broiler pork; however it tasted like it had been sitting out for a while (since it was a little cold). The rice was on point today woo! Love good rice, there fish sauce is different, liked that. Hmm what else... Mmm that's about it. It was an okay experience the server/host is not the most experienced but he gets the job done. 4 stars if I would have had a hot meal, 5 if the service was awesome.
If you haven't been here you're missing one of St Louis's best lunches! $9.95 for a 2 course lunch with drink included! WOW!!!

I have not had good pho since I was stationed in California. With the changing of the seaons and fall upon us I have been in the mood for some good pho. The reviews on this place were did not inspire confidence but it was Sunday afternoon and my choices were limited. I was hoping to be surprised. I was not. When entering the resturaunt I got a wordless greeting to sit down. The table I got was dirty and sticky. Not off to a great start. Looking around the resturaunt it was obvious that nobody had cared about it for a few years. I was still hoping that looks would be decieving and that I would be surprised. A young girl came up to us and took our order. When I asked what was in a specific dish, she obviously didn't have a clue. Her answer was "a little bit of everything like pork, beef, chicken and other stuff." I placed my order for that and was then told to choose from those. I piked beef and ignored the ignorance. My friend with me had never had pho and now it was her time to order. She also asked about a specific dish she was interested and got a general answer like mine. I let her know she has never had pho before and would like to know more, the answer we received was "are you sure you want that?" We are adventurous eaters but to be asked that question was a first for me. Orders complete our drinks came. Both tasted like dirty dish soap. The water and the soft drink. When aske to have it replaced I was met with a roll of the eyes and a sigh. I must have interrupted her iPhone time as for our entire visit she spent more time on it than taking care of what few customers there was. Poor me... I was still expecting to be surprised. Our food came. Both dishes were bland and had very little flavor. Nobody was impressed (other than the waitress/hostest with her phone) and both dishes went unfinished. Even with the huge craving I had for pho. I recomend that if you are in the mood for pho, skip this establishment. I know we are limited on locations that have that dish here in the Boise area. But do NOT do this to yourself. I can not speak for their other dishes as nothing was tried, but this is NOT the place for pho. Move on. Pho aside, I do not recommend this place and will not be back myself. It has the posiblities to be a good place but some where along the line it seems they have lost the love for food and for service.

This place is my go to whenever I'm hungry. And don't want to cook. (Often) Their goat is to die for. The mongoo is also excellent. Ask for their smoothies. Owner and all workers are so nice. Pay them a visit. Will not be disappointed.

When there for the first time this week. Excellent food, authentic and fresh. Staff was also very nice and most of all the Buffett is great value for money! Highly recommend and will be back for sure...

YOU MUST EAT HERE! My husband and I were wow'ed by the food and service here! It's a tiny yet charming BYO restaurant with amazing food! We had reservations at 6pm on a Wednesday and it was PACKED. Reservations are a must as we have seen people get turned away. Our favorites of the night were the antipasto siciliano, gnocchi alla argentiera, tagliatelle al limone (get it with bottarga), and the special which was orata, quite possibly the best fish dish I have ever had. IMO it's better than Osteria or Vetri in Philly and the service is always spot on. Will definitely be coming here many times :) Edit: It's unfortunate that people give this place a 1 star just because they couldn't secure a seat. Make reservations ahead of time, even for a weeknight!

We dined here for the first time tonight and it was phenomenal. I'm vegan but the rest of my family isn't, so normally eating out together is a struggle. The owner was soooo friendly and he went over the menu to help me figure out what I could eat. There are a lot of vegan options and everything we got was amazing. My two year old is pretty picky and even she was happy with the food. You just can't beat a good Mom and Pop restaurant with great food and friendly service. This place is a new favorite and we can't wait to go back! I will be sure to update my review with pictures, the next time we go back.

Sky Cafe, I'm so sad that I'm moving away and leaving you. I came here on Saturday with my sister and it was like being transported back to Medan, Indonesia. We were the only non-Indonesians in the place. You MUST get the sate ayam (chicken sate), and the kwetiau goreng (fried noodles). Both taste just like the food that I used to eat in Indonesia. Sitting in the restaurant and listening to the bahasa Indonesia and stuffing myself with Indonesian food was definitely the highlight of my weekend. I also love how affordable this place is. Lunch for two came to $12.
Simply wonderful! Very courteous service. Perfect balance of coconut and hot spice. Appropriately portioned for half the price.

Let me also caveat that I went on Open Mic night. That was my first mistake, although I really like the decor and the general feel of the place Open Mic night ruined that because all of the people who stayed for Open Mic night were no longer eating chicken or never ordered chicken to begin with were taking up the seats. Meanwhile my group of 6 was there having ordered 3 lbs of chicken and Mac and Cheese. So we start eating and talking about our meal and then we get shushed. That is right we got shushed by the manager or greeter when I am pretty sure out of the 20 other people there, we were the only ones actually eating chicken. We were forced to sit directly in front of the players because all of the non-chicken eating customers were in the booths. This is the main reason I am giving this place 1 star. That was a pretty crappy way to alienate your only customers eating chicken. Aside from that, the front counter service was friendly and courteous. That one experience just poisoned my overall opinion of this place. I thought the chicken was pretty alright with the sauces being the best part of the meal. The Mac and Cheese was breaded but was bland and needed a bit more flavor and probably less breading. The food on its own and overall restaurant feel would have rated a 2 stars. They have a cool drink selection including cock cola (named after the rooster) and some hip natural colas. This place is worth a try but I would recommend a lunch time trip to avoid any Open Mic night concerns and you can make your own judgement. They just started up so maybe they are still working out recipes and what the final food will be.

I was in the mood for a gyro/falafel type sandwich for lunch on a lazy Saturday so I decided to try this place for take-out on the recommendation of my fellow Yelpers. Needless to say, I was not disappointed. I went with a Wilson's sandwich, fries and an order of grape leaves. The Wilson's sandwich is genius. Why have two separate sandwiches of meat or falafel when you can combine them into one awesome one? The sanwich came with grilled chicken, falafel, veggies, tzaiki sauce, olives, hummus and special hot sauce all wrapped in a homemade pita. It was messy, but it was delicious. The fries tasted good, but were soft and soggy probably due to the stryofoam container they were transported in during my walk home. I could've done without them. I was going to get a piece of pistachio baklava ($1.25) but only had 50 cents left to my name. Next time you will be mine sweet baklava... On a side-note, besides the "Wilson's", they also have a sandwich called the "Angelo Cataldi" which I guess is a salute to the venerable figure of Philly sports radio and such notable events like Wing Bowl. Right on Bitar's, right on. .

I had the lemongrass chicken vermicelli. Spicy and really perfectly seasoned. More fish sauce please! The chicken wasn't dry and rubbery as you typically find with this dish. I ordered the grilled pork rolls. They're fresh rolls with grilled pork and they come with fish sauce. Great! I tried a fried egg roll with pork. These were some of the best I have ever had. I also tried a fried chicken wing. These came with a couple sauces and were just plain unbelievable. Crispy and impossible to stop eating. The food here is creative and thoughtful even though sometimes uneven. Nice menu and good service.

This is hands down my favorite restaurant in St. Louis. My roommate and I have made it a weekly tradition to come here... you can't go wrong with anything on their menu. This food is incredibly authentic and delicious. The owners make this food even better, though, as they are some of the nicest people I have met. They make their food with love!

Well crafted innovative offerings in a neat space. Visited for pri fix brunch. Tuna bagel and shrimp curry small plates were fantastic and inspired. Did not try cocktails but looked great and coffee was delicious. Overall service was good, but our server was exceptional.
As good as I remember :D I left Tampa 4 months ago, and was glad to be back. Got the short ribs rice that I love so much, and they brought back memories.

We were very excited to be trying this Thai restaurant that had a good number of reviews and 4 stars. So......I'm not sure what part of Thailand the owners are from but there is NO love in there food. We ordered Tom Yum and it was bland so much so that we needed to add salt.....yuck!! I've traveled all over Thailand and this restaurant has dumbed down the true essence of real Thai food. The soup was lacking Tamarind and Fish Sauce. We then ordered Panang Curry with pork. It came to us and at first I thought we ordered vegetarian Panang because except for the 6 pieces of pork the entire dish was filled with green beans. Come on.....you are using this vegetable as a filler!!! Give me pork!!!! The sauce also was lacking so much flavor. If we did not order to go I would have returned everything. Not so Thai!!

The Caprese sandwich was pretty tasty, if $8.50 for a sandwich sits ok with you. It's also a cute place. As other reviews mention, however, they won't give you a glass of water to go with your meal. You have to buy a bottle of it or go without. I have a problem with bottled water in general, and with a restaurant that skips an amenity most restaurants offer without charge, so... meh.
I'm not into writing long reviews. I'm not a fan of duck. I never order my food. I got the duck. It was amazing! Everything was great. So was the service.

I've downloaded yelp just to tell people about this place. Smiley's is the best falafel I've had. He's great to come chat with and he's never made me anything less than delicious. He is committed to making you happy and takes the time to create amazing flavors in his food. Go. Eat and be happy.

Going to Ali Baba's has become a NO tradition. Originally stumbled on during a late night food run, it's become our regular grab a bite place when in NO. Basically for the price of a street dog, you can have a tasty gyro with a squeeze of rooster sauce if you please.
We loved it. 2nd time. Food fresh and yummy. Great price and BYOB. Ask about the baklava. Yummy gyros and fresh veg. Going back soon.
I come here a lot. Just had a birthday here too. Love the girls dancing and the customer service is amazing and quick. Drinks are always so good here and the mood and setting is perfect!!!

Best thai food in south Tampa, I go at least once a week and bring everyone I know here! Everything is fantastic, and I highly recommend the duck fried rice and phad woonsin with seafood. The portions are huge and they are able to accommodate everyone's heat preferences!
Surprisingly tasty! Great pho and grilled meat dishes. I'm definitely coming back.
Very good. I was impressed. Hummus and pita were amazing. Didn't love their fries but there was a ton in the bucket I got with my combo. Will be back.

First of all, some people might think of this restaurant as Mexican, but it's not! I found this gem as I was walking from the Music City Center for the Wizard World Comic Con. The restaurant is somewhat small, but it's delicious food makes up for it. As some people (mostly my family and few friends) know, I LOVE calamari! So when I saw it on the menu, I had to get it. It came out crispy, not rubbery (like I've had it at other locations), encrusted with herbs and cilantro! Yummy! I then went on to have the Ropa Vieja, which is cuban-styled {very well seasoned} pork flank steak. I loved this item. I Had a pina colda (of course with rum....they have a "virgin" style, good for kids). There were some many good items on the menu that the next time I go down, I'm going to have to bring a few friends to sample different food items. Any volunteers.

This was possibly the best Indian lunch buffet we've had in the Indy area. Fo starters, the naan was fresh and delicious, and the mint chutney was definitely homemade. They also had the best selection we have seen, with several vegetarian and vegan dishes as well. The saag was creamy and delicious, and the goat curry was tasty as well. They had a great dessert selection, too, with mango yogurt, gulab jamun, rice pudding, etc. Finally, we received the best service we've experienced at an Indian buffet, and our server was super accommodating of our toddler.

since I just finished bemoaning the downhill slide of another Thai place, I feel it's only fair to give Erawan the credit it deserves. To me, this is the best Thai food in Center City and I've made a point to sample all six or seven options. the lunch special is beautifully presented, filling, a great value and best of all, it's really tasty. it can get a little crowded during the lunch rush some days - I've found Fridays are a little lighter or just going closer to 1 p.m.

Not impressed. I love their other locations in Metairie but it bothers me that everything is more expensive at this location. I can't believe they charged me for a to go order!! That's crazy. I'm going to stick with Magasin Restaurant instead.

I've stopped here twice on a Sunday for the lunch buffet. I like the complimentary tea and mango lassi and the food is average. However, each time I've been there a woman (possibly the owner/manager) has been on her cell phone talking nonstop while seating people, while filling water glasses and even while checking people out when leaving. She can't put the phone down to greet or say thank you? And the entire time we were eating she was on the phone in the back of the restaurant and wasn't very quiet in her conversation. I think next time I try one of the other Indian restaurants in the area.
Great atmosphere. Service was so so. Food was not good. Rubbery calamari. Bread and oil on table was plain. Red sauce was bland.

This was exactly what i was looking for. Tasty food in a nice 8 table small Thai place. The pot sticker app and pad thai hit the spot. At 3 sicy it was hot but did not hide the flavor. The raggoon and egg roll as part of the special were tiny... but for $1 well worth the money and a nice addition.
So happy they now have this great restaurant in Tucson. We would drive to Scottsdale for the original. The food is the same quality of ingredients and the ambiance is excellent. Love the Soltani.

Thought we were going to a nice restaurant, but the overall feel was douchey club. Jimmy was a great server, the food was on point, but the whole vibe was very douchetastic. There was a 4 year old sitting at the bar. I'm not kidding. He may have been 3. Seems like they cater to douchebags and whores. Too bad because the food is good, and at least Jimmy is a good server.
Came here with a group. Good food. Sambosa was delicious. Chicken kabobs were great and flavored nicely. Friendly staff. Good place to try out afghan food

Had very good salmon wrapped in a grape leaf in my last visit and tonight my wife and I ordered the fix price menu. She had Pad Thai with chicken and I had Thai Basil with meat. I had Thai Ravioli Soup and Thai Dumpling. As usual all of the food was excellent but not too filling.

In a word...AMAZING!!! I've been eating here for years and even though I'm now 2 states away, anytime I find myself in Philly I find myself in Sister Muhammad's kitchen. Have you ever tasted love in food? Eaten a meal where you know the person picked out all the best ingredients and served to you what they would serve to themselves and their family? That's the magic of this place, not to mention the innovative dishes that they've created like the Fish Fried rice. I recommend you eat in, take some orders to go and never, ever forget dessert like the banana pudding and butternut squash pie, which I like to take home and warm in the oven. Also, the place is sparkling clean and the staff friendly and helpful. It's not fast food, it's good food!

Went here a couple weeks ago, as it is a newer establishment and we like to support local business. First off, this place was formerly a Smashburger and basically nothing has changed in terms of decorations and ambiance (there's a few random rustic signs up, but it kind of seems out of place given the contemporary feel). Anyway, service was awful! We waited about 10-15 min to even get noticed after we were seated and then went up to the hostess counter to get their attention. The waitress promptly came over and apologized stating that the hostess never notified her that she had a table. Based on this, there seems to be lack of communication between all employees. All of the employees should be communicating and helping each other out and whatever personal matters they have should be put aside. However, after this hiccup, the service got better and the waitress was pretty attentive. Food was pretty decent (not mind-blowing but acceptable). All in all, I'd chose this over ihop.

Love the food, good and so delicious.We drive all the way from DC and stop here for lunch..bit hard to find the place specially if u not from PA area.i'm definitely come back what ever I got the change

Came with my kids and a friend, my children were so thirsty. It took over 10 minutes for water, had it been sooner they would have been more content. The owner/ server neglected us and acted as though we did not exist. I'm appalled, having come alone with a different experience service wise . The choices for Vietnamese in the area are slim. My children are US born Vietnamese-American and love the ethnic food. I'm not sure if it was the kids or a male friend who he made stereotypical assumptions regarding. Needless to say now both times the Pho was unimpressive and the rest kind of followed. I will not be back. Shame, because it's close.

I order takeout from Ekta pretty regularly - My cravings are frequent and intense but I pat myself on the back after each visit. Tantalizing flavors, wonderfully aromatic aromas, and hearty, highly satisfying menu items are commonplace. My current favorites include Lamb Chettinad, Chicken Korma, Ekta vegetables, baigan bharta, and garlic naan. Each and every friend, family member, foodie, and fearless leader I've shared an ekta meal with has been consumed by south indian spice & everything nice and is eagerly awaiting their next ekta experience. Don't be upset but sometimes I enjoy savoring Ekta dishes alone - I love all of you but I'm addicted to Ekta leftovers - especially for lunch the following day. I may get Ekta tonight....it would be the third time in less than two weeks and there is nothing at all wrong with that! If your taste buds are craving some new flavors or wish to take a journey across the globe, I highly recommend giving Ekta a shot. You will leave with your very own Ekta-fied needs and desires - and as your relationship with ekta matures, your tastebuds will always get lots of attention and remain young at heart. Ekta OVER all other Indian restaurants around the Main Line. You will be amazed by all of the flavors!! This place is a gem and everyone should try it!!

This place use to be the best for gyros. But upon my recent visits it has gone down hill. I get the same thing all the time and made me smile and here is what I'm now sadly eating. the spinach rotini that was robust and Tangy is now dull bland and unsavory. The gyro deluxe that was the epitome of the deli is now sad and disheartening. The lettuce use to be crisp and crunchy is now soft and cabbage like. The feta was pungently great that made your mouth scream "YES" is now feeling like they bought it from the cheap store and left in the car for a few days. The pita once was airy and filling now feels like smashed bread that isn't even cooked. And now for the meat it was the best in St. Louis every bite was was delightful and you could taste the lamb with the longest after taste even an hour later you felt like you had just eaten now tastes 3rd rate and wanted to quickly drink water to make dull the after taste. I'm am saddened to write this and hope it's just a food slump they are in and soon explode the flavors they once had. I will eat there again in the later months and update this if it's better. The next time I'll make sure to eat there so I can ask them what happened.

Had a late lunch at Lilly's today. The place was pacjed at 2pm ... and after having a meal here, I know why. We only had two dishes. .. spicy tofu and Pho Ga (chicken). The spicy tofu was excellent, tender, tasty with a spicy flavor that was perfect as served. The Pho is also very very good... it comes to the table piping hot with fresh sprouts and basil to add as desire. I found that a few good doses of rooster sauce (sriracha) brought the flavor to just where I like it. Final verdict: we both agreed that we would willingly order the same again... but will try other dishes as well. Service was very good, courteous and efficient and Lilly is a great hostess.

Wonderful! Food is absolutely Delicious- the atmosphere is Beachy and relaxed- the breeze is always blowing down this street- service is excellent- Live Beachy music on Sundays!!! Felt as if we were in the Carribean- Mary is the wonderful hostess who will make you feel at home and serve you drinks while you wait for menus - she HIGHLY recommended the mimosa flights - so good! It's 4 different mimosas flavored with 4 different juices- They also have beer flights - Perfect for brunch! The Tex mex Migas were to die for- I didn't expect so much out if eggs but the tortillas and green and red bell peppers and onions made the dish. Get them with chorizo !!! They also offer many types of hot sauce - The Cuban sandwich was perfect- I told them I had to catch a plane and they cooked my brunch FAST to make sure I got to eat.. That was priceless. COME HERE!!
Fresh and made to order pho. Other dishes are amazing. Recommend #70 pork chop to die for. Definitely becoming a regular here. Did I mention prices are very reasonable and portions are generous?? ;)

Wow! My lips just stop tingling from the spicy awesomeness that was the chili noodle. Delish! We also had the Panang Curry and the fried spring rolls. All the food was fresh and yummy. The atmosphere was really light, airy and open. I guess I haven't been inside this space since it was a coffee shop over a decade ago and it still had a house configuration back then. So the renovation may not be new to this restaurant but I really like it. The menu has a lot of variety without being too long. And they state that they will customize any dish even making stuff vegan. The Chili Noodles normally have chicken or beef, but I got them with fried tofu, but I also could have picked soft. It looks like they have a liquor license now since behind the bar they're was the biggest bottle of knob creek that I've ever seen. mmmm bourbon. Also, the name is really Singha Song Thai so I'm guessing they aren't affiliated with the Singha downtown. I submitted the change to our Yelp overlords so I guess it will changed eventually.
First off, Pho is fo loners. I ate my giant amazing pho by myself, alongside 3 other loners, it was great pho!!! I mean it guys... I'll be coming back again like tomorrow. #pholoners

We stumbled upon this place by a complete accident while looking for sone where to have dinner while visiting my daughter in Philadelphia. Between the experience , music , decorations , hospitality I have to rate it s perfect five stars.

Still one of my favorite places to eat. Everything I've eaten has been delicious, the staff are friendly, and the atmosphere is quiet and homey. Every person I've taken there to eat has enjoyed the experience and asks to go back. Would definitely recommend!
This place is way better than Byblos. I love the wraps and the salad. Good hummus too. Will go back.

I am giving this restuarant one star because we did not dine there. We attempted to though. We showed up on a Saturday night about 8:30 pm. The parking lot was full but we did not see a line or anything to look like there was a wait. When we walked inside the music downstairs was so loud it sounded like a Salsa club. There was no host to greet us. Finally a man came up to us and told us they were booked for the night and that there was "going to be a long wait". Uh okay... He did mention we were welcomed to sit at the end of the bar if we wanted to. Who wants to eat a nice dinner at the end of a bar? We will not be back to try to eat here.

The food was great and the staff was amazing. I had the Drunkin Noodle with chicken and my wife had the Pad Thai with pork. Both dishes were huge portions and delicious. The owner came out and talked to us about the different dishes they offer and made sure we were enjoying everything we ordered. Definitely coming back soon!

It is indeed possible to fall in love with the owners of a restaurant you love. This is the case with Parisa's, owned by a Persian couple who are the very definition of hospitality. Once a week on Saturdays Parisas serves a buffet between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. Krista and I had planned to get there by 1:30 p.m., but each of us being the less than perfect time managers that we are, it was clear we weren't going to get there until 2:15 p.m. I called the restaurant to ask if it would be alright for us to arrive this late and was told, "Yeeeasss, shhhhuuuuure," by Parisa who then said, "I will make fresh kabobs for you!" Wow. That made me feel special and we hadn't even left the house. We were greated with hugs and excitement, as if we'd come for a visit. There were four other parties seated and we were told to choose any table we liked and then to help ourselves when ready. Krista gushed about being new to Persian food and both Mr. and Mrs. Parisa took her under their wing, but Mr. Parisa made Krista his special project, explaining the food and the sauces to her in some detail, and even dishing up combinations of sauces and foods he thought she might like. There are no strange organ meats here, no odd body parts such as hooves.... no no no!!! Everything is quite amenable to the American palate. Everything we wanted was our's for the asking and Krista couldn't be more correct that the Parisas make you feel both like family and royalty. Who wouldn't want to come here as often as they could afford it. You leave feeling pampered, satisfied, and dare I say loved? Yes -- love is the word.
By far my favorite place to go for a quick bite. The choclatey turtle cheesecake changed my life. The girl who helped me was very friendly despite the place being packed.

I like how you can see the cook , it's looks nice and clean, cute seating area. The people working was great. The food was good and tasty plus fresh . Just wish they devein the shrimps. Next time I will get the beef. I will be back

Chiang Mai is one of my very favorite restaurants in Indy, but I was disappointed to learn that they are under new ownership, and that a number of my favorite menu items will be discontinued. I cannot fathom why the new owners would want to drastically alter the menu so far as the remove the entire noodle section. This used to be my go-to restaurant, but that will probably be changing.

I love to go here for lunch. I've not traveled to India (yet) so I can't speak to the authenticity of the food. But I do see diners who appear to be of Indian descent, which is a positive sign. The lunch buffet is huge, and nearly everyone can find something they enjoy. My favorites are the chicken tikka masala, mushroom saag, and saag paneer. I've actually tried to create a few of their dishes at home, with varying levels of success. The waiters can be a bit slow on refilling drinks, but otherwise are generally friendly.

First time coming in tonight and our meal was great!! We ordered Korean fried chicken, pork and beef ramen, all of which were absolutely fantastic! Staff was very friendly and took great care of us! Can't wait to make this a regular spot!

I went to a catered party recently where they served Kalamata's deliciousness. White and wheat pitas with plates of hummus. Delicious Greek salad, tasty marinated chicken, and a GIANT platter of stuffed grape leaves abounded. Yummy. I've also had excellent dine in experiences with the folks at Kalamata's and can recommend the gyros (which, while apparently is street food, is my favorite Greek treat). The people that work here are very friendly and the food always tastes incredibly fresh (they bake their pitas fresh every day! Maybe they could teach me...) As an added bonus, oftentimes they've got live music at this location!

Pros: Fast servce Wide vareity Decent tableware Cons: Bland, Americanized renditions of Vietnamese food Bland, bland, bland I miss really good pho. And spring rolls. I'm guessing the clientele that frequents this place are people who don't like spicy, or spices that would be used in any decent Vietnamese restaurant. Or, they live/work nearby. In either case, I was really sad after my meal, especially because we went to see 'The Blind Side' afterward. Dammit - that's just money lost to mediocre all the way around.

Went here because it was well reviewed, and it was the worst hookah experience we've ever had! We all had one mediocre drink we didn't even finish (since it's a one-drink minimum per person) and we weren't even able to finish the house special hookah as two of us started to feel extremely sick. Ruined our nights.... It was not a great atmosphere- almost no space between tables, uncomfortable for any intimate conversation, strangers kept jumping into our conversation. But it might have been worth it for the affordable hookah had we not gotten sick. First time in several years of going to hookah bars any of us has had a bad experience. Don't know why this place is so well-reviewed.
Just about every restaurant in New Orleans have amazing food. they use just the right spices to dazzle your taste buds. I highly recommend....
The server is attentive. The food is decent. However compare with the other choices nearby, their buffet has less option.
Nice little spot, although it's in an unassuming strip mall behind Psghettis! I had the Deluxe Gyro and it was delicious! Very generous portions and fast friendly service.
The real deal! True authentic Greek food in a cozy casual atmosphere. Fresh and delicious just like Yia Yia makes it!

An update on Nadia's for any folks interested. It's been several months since we've eaten at Nadia's so we were rather curious to see if we'd find any noticeable complacency...Maybe the service will not be as attentive or the food won't be as good as remembered resulting in an evening's disappointment. . Well, I'm pleased to report this was not the case with our recent visit. We joined another couple at 7:30 on a Saturday night. No reservations were required .. Of the 12 or so tables maybe 2 were unoccupied when we arrived. The food and service was just as good as remembered. I had the Spicy chicken stir fry with mixed vegetables in a spicy Thai basil curry sauce. Excellent! (I ate it slowly because I didn't want it to end).. One of our party had the Crispy duck with mixed vegetables in a sweet plum sauce. He said he had made the right choice.. Empty plates all around..We weren't rushed although the service was attentive.. Our bill was $62 pre-tip for the four of us. We all thought our meals were very good. Easy parking, situated right next to the Lansdale train station. We'll be back! .

Way too expensive for cart food, the guy is sometimes annoying and hard to understand, it stinks the whole block up with garlic smell, you have no idea what he's putting in your platter or sandwich, the line moves slower than a glacier, and it's the best food in the city. Someone once asked me since I love it so much if it would be my death row meal and my reply was if I'm on death row it's probably because I killed someone for standing between me and this falafel.

Best gyro I've ever had, every bite was banging. The people who own it are awesome they gave me and my friend a free smoothie because it was our first time there, smoothie was great too. All the food looks like it is made and prepared the original way and you can tell when you enjoying your meal.
Fez Moroccan was absolutely delicious. The eight course meal is shared among everyone sitting at the table and you eat with your hands. The chicken was so tender it literally fell off the bones.

We had a table of 5, and everyone loved the food! We ordered several small plates which were all delicious. The burrata, mushrooms, duck, and octopus were especially good. Also, Chrissy took great care of us! The drinks were great as well. The Negroni was top notch!
It's back...and the new digs are beautiful! Same warm service, all the old favorites...life is good. Sure to be discovered by locals soon.

I was in the neighborhood for a lunch meeting and upon learning of my love of sushi suggested this place. It was perfect. The hostess was pleasant and the waitress was quick, knowledgeable, friendly and eager to help. But that's not why you go to Fulin's. I had one of the lunch plate specials, sashimi I think. I upgraded to the seaweed salad which was fabulous-perhaps the best I've ever had. The miso was good, and the plate of sashimi was outstanding. This is authentic, Japanese style sashimi. It's not the thin slice of fish on a big lump of rice like most round-eyes associate with sushi. This is a plate of thick slices of various fish. I ate every piece, even the ones I couldn't identify. They were all good. The wasabi was great. Everything was great, except that I wanted to order three more servings of the plate, and that would have embarrassed my colleagues. Go to Fulin's if you like sushi.
This is my favorite Thai place in the Tampa bay area. I've tried everything close by and that's right....a food truck wins!! Nice, friendly staff, fresh made to order food, great flavor, good price.

I loooove Northern Chinese food. It's the only time you'll see me recommending a Chinese restaurant, at least when it comes to Edmonton's options. Okay fine, Shanghai 456 would make the cut but technically, that's Shanghainese food. Either way, Wheat Garden Noodle & Dumpling Bazaar quietly opened up last month, taking over the old red house from Old Szechuan, which moved it's digs to Whyte Ave. Anyways, I was stoked to hear about a second Northern Chinese restaurant opening in town! Finally, an alternative to driving all the way to Noodle Feast. The interior received a much needed face lift. The walls are freshly painted white and gives the place a much friendlier vibe. Don't expect too much though, there's still plastic mats covering the tables. Typical Chinese décor. There's also a small TV set up playing random Chinese shows that you can only chuckle at. Who cares though. Most importantly, would it live up to the glory of Noodle Feast? The menu consists of noodles, dumplings and snacks. What I like is that for the noodle section, there's four different styles for you to choose from. Just tell them what type you want when you order them. Don't forget. Go with the wide, flat ones, those are my fav (the third one). Service is very friendly. The couple (I believe) working are a bit shy but they are quite attentive. Nice that their hours changed since my original visit - they're open for lunch now. Trip #1 - Beef noodle soup ((#101) ($11.99) - beef with green onion, leak and daikon. The broth is simple and to me, it tastes herbal/medicinal/healthy. You won't be blown away but if you're looking for a bit more kick, add some of their chili oil to your bowl. - Wide noodles (#109) ($11.99) - wide noodles mixed with Northwest Chinese style spicy chicken, potato, green pepper and onions. This is one of their specialty dishes and have to say this was my favourite dish of the night. Nice bit of heat to the dish, super flavourful and the noodles had a great bite/toothsomeness to them. -Lamb rice pilaf (#303) ($12.99) - with lamb, carrot and onion. Think biryani but replace with Northern Chinese style spices. Again, another of their specialties and it delivered. Lamb was nicely spiced and flavours were just umami. - Dumplings all in one ($13.99) - you can either pick one type of dumpling (six types to choose from) or if you want an assortment, you can go with the all in one option. We choose the latter and you get a colorful platter of dumplings, 15 to be exact. The dumplings were pretty good - moist, tender, and juicy. My friends liked it so much we ordered another round. Trip #2 - I had to come back a second time to try a couple more of their dishes before making a verdict. Bbop and I checked them out Friday for lunch. - Cold steamed noodles (#301) ($5.99) - comes with cucumber, bean sprouts and gluten. I wanted to try this on my first visit but they don't enjoy cold dishes. Their loss, this dish was doooooooope. So many great things coming from this little dish - the noodles are perfect with a great bite and texture to them that's different than their other hand-made noodles. Tantalizing, prepare for a bit of numbness to reach your lips. The cucumbers and bean sprouts help to cool things off a bit. - Ground beef noodles (#110) ($10.99) - comes with bok choy, peas and chicken broth. This noodle soup was BOMB. Our favourite dish for sure. The broth was heavenly - almost peanut like but quite light and again, the slightest level of numbness. I was pleasantly surprised as I wasn't expecting this to even have a soup base. What I've learned so far - order their noodle soups with the "hot" icons beside it. - Lamb noodle soup (#102) ($12.99) - with black fungus, kelp, dried lily and goji berries. I thought this one might be different than the beef noodle soup we originally tried but the broth was identical. Bbop wasn't a fan but at least it gave us a contrasting flavour. For what it's worth, he kept on going back to the other bowl. I really like the black fungus and kelp in the dish. Fungus is just texturally pleasant. Kelp was new to me - it's a seaweed, which reminded me a bit of Hawaii and their numerous algae/seaweeds that they throw into their cuisine. - Jelly noodle (#302) ($5.99) - stir fried jelly noodle with bean sprouts and vegetables. Thought they might have forgot about this one but they brought out it out piping hot. Poor Bbop, what a rookie, didn't wait and burnt his tongue. I'm not kidding when I say it came out hot.This was my first time having this type of jelly cubes - it was more like a starch jelly. If you've had lo bac go (turnip cake) before, it has that same mushy consistency. Surprisingly good with the chili flakes but a half size would have been more than enough to share. Oh well, nothing wrong with leftovers. Wheat Garden has "hidden gem" written all over it. Hope the word gets out soon and that more specialized Chinese cuisine gems starts to pop up in the future!
Was delivered quickly. They did mess up my order. Not bad for delivery Chinese food in Southern NJ.

This place is OUTSTANDING. It is a bit of a dive, but it was clean. Whoever was in the kitchen today was FRICKIN AMAZING! After a horrible experience at some Ventura Thai place I reluctantly tried some cocoanut milk based soup and I swear I couldn't stop eating it... it was heaven in a bowl. I HIGHLY recommend this place but hope it doesn't become too trendy and crowded.

The decor was nice and the service was prompt. Sadly, the dishes lacked flavor and the desert was the frozen kind that you find at the Asian market. The seafood was definitely not fresh. I will not be returning. I recall the dishes being much tastier years ago.

So, my first visit to Olio was interesting, the food tasted good but that is the only thing that did.... Service was slow, waitress was a soft talker and my party of 3 had no clue what was being said, plastic chairs that felt like it circumcision in progress. Again food tasted good but very small portions.... Won't be going there ever again
Great experience! Wonderfully nice staff and amazing food. Hot fresh and ready for takeout in under 20 mins. I ordered the red curry and fresh rolls with chicken, must try this place!!

Best Indian Buffet I've ever been to. Hands down. It's hard to rate a buffet without writing 10 pages on it. I could easily, but I won't. This places crushes every Indian place that I've ever been to, and I've been to ALOT. This is my absolute favorite. It's very rare that I give place 5 stars, but I'd give six if I could. Stop reading now and go!

Come here whenever I'm visiting from NYC the bartenders are always extremely friendly. The clientele is a huge range from mid 20s-30s late night to an older crowd earlier. Cocktails and food are always on point. Always meet great people here and unlike a lot of bars nearby excluding canopy has a great upscale atmosphere where everyone feels welcome. Great outdoor seating as well

Ate at the Kabob House last night. The decor was great, the food was excellent (and healthy), and the service was very attentive. I predict great things for this restaurant in its new location. Congratulations and keep the good times coming!

Where to begin with this terrible dining experience??? The premise of this place is great, but the execution fell very very very short. The food was good, but definitely not memorable. There was no depth of flavors, just a trendy menu. They were NOT busy and yet the service was terrible from start to finish: After being seated waited almost 10 minute for our waiter. Drinks were slow to come. The food eventually started to arrive at our tiny table was literally dropped off by their food runner who delivered us the wrong foods and no one ever came back to our table to check on food or drinks. When we finally decide to leave I had to get up and ask the hostess for our check. She sent a manager over to us who apologized and took off the cost of one appetizer. Still didn't make it worth our time or money. Don't waste your money, this place falls very short.

Reasons you should go to Mo'ziki: - It's good, fresh food in a fast casual setting. Think Moe's but with a greek twist. You can build your meal in a variety of ways to satisfy your Greek/Mediterranean taste buds. - The tomatoes are actually RED. That sentence alone you make your mouth water. - The lemon rice is divine. In a wrap or in a rice bowl, it's that one thing that I can get there that I can't anywhere else. - The gyro meat is tender, juicy and perfectly seasoned. The grilled chicken is cooked to perfection. - They have a great selection of fountain drinks. Four iced teas? I found heaven. - The kitchen is open so you can see everything being prepped (think Five Guys / Moe's). What can I say, I like seeing where my food comes from. - Damn fine hummus. - The rice bowls (and possibly the salads) come in microwavable containers. Yes, I take them home, wash them and reuse them. This is a perk for me. - Comfortable and open dining area. Get in line, order your food, get your food and sit down to a clean table. I've yet to see litter or a messy table. - It's a local small business. Coming out of the gate, they have their branding LOCKED DOWN. You walk in and think this is a franchise but no, this was all them.

Their Thai food is the best I've had yet. The service was a bit off and so was the appetizer but the pad thai, duck curry, and tom yum really made up for it. It is a bit pricey but what could you expect when you're in Santa Barbara.

This place offers a good alternative to burgers and fried chicken. So if we were in the mood for fast food, but wanted to avoid a trip to the usual chains, Dooners would do the trick. That said, the food was nothing to rave about. It was just different. We went on a Saturday night and the kids working the counter seemed a little "out of it". Didn't seem excited to be there. They were talking more to each other while preparing our food than they were to us. They were unenthusiastic about answering questions (maybe because they are always answering questions like, "what is dooner?"). Be careful to restrict their use of cabbage. It has a powerful flavor and they will literally smother your food in it. So... would we go back. Maybe. But we won't be craving it, and we won't go out of our way to eat there.

So the atmosphere isn't that great. Kind of like a cafeteria that plays TMZ. I'm a vegetarian so there isn't much for me here. Which should have been obvious due to the "7 course beef" offering. I got the lemongrass tofu which was ok....I won't be returning to this place.

Their smoothies keep getting better and better. I highly recommend the taro smoothie with boba. It's wonderful. Do not go here when it's busy and that is starting to be every evening. My food came out five minutes before my friend's and we finally got a water refill after asking at the end of the meal. I ordered noodles, paid a dollar extra than my friend's, and it was this fried onion thing. Kinda disappointing. I would go back for the drinks though.

A GREAT addition to the neighborhood. Wonderful ambiance, pastries, tea/coffee and lunch. We sat near the kitchen and I wanted to eat everything that was brought out! I didn't know what most of it was but it all looked delicious! I look very forward to my next visit, and especially to sitting on the patio when it's warmer. Also, there is a free parking lot across the street (Suraya customers only) which is a huge bonus. My only complaint is that they aren't open for dinner.

Just had lunch at this location. I typically choose Masala dishes. But the owner was super helpful in helping me select something just as tasty. I had a jumbo shrimp dish that was awesome! They have lunch specials until 3. Dinner starts at 4. Definitely a neighborhood gem!

Ate there tonight based on a review from a coworker. The server was attentive and very helpful with advice on meal selection. Everything was delicious. This is truly the best Indian food I have eaten in a long time. Give this place a try and you will not be sorry. Think we just found our new favorite Indian restaurant.

My girlfriend was raving about Philly Indonesian food so we finally got the chance to make the drive down the turnpike from Jersey...WOW, unbelievably glad we did! To preface this, I have eaten at numerous Indonesian places in Queens, NY, and am a big fan of Asian comfort food (doesn't matter if it is Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Malaysian, or anything else I missed!) and have seen too many mediocre bowls of "noodles". Not gonna lie, the area threw me off a bit. Im not used to having to park a larger car backing into a tiny spot in a cramped street. I felt like my mirrors were going to become the casualties of the six young kids playing ball up and down the small row. The area was a little suspect, as we already passed over another place due to its really shady look neighborhood. I will venture for good food any day, but sometimes instinct tells you to keep moving! I gotta say, walking in felt like I had grown up down the block. It just emanated that local, unpretentious, warm feeling that is lost in some of the shiny, new, plasticky restaurants I see so often in North Jersey. 10 or so tables, small staff, a refrigerator filled with desserts, and the familiar smells of the feast to come fill your senses. We ordered fried wontons, mie komplit (#1 on noodle page), the spicy salted fish entree, and the pork combination (#18 on entrees page). The wontons were surprisingly thin and flavorful. Very crunchy, definitely different than the ones you usually get at a corner Chinese spot. The mie komplit comes with egg noodles, roasted pork, and ground beef amongst some bright greens and fried onions. You are given a separate bowl with chicken broth and some fish cake/meatballs floating playfully in it. It's up to you to either douse your noodles into a full on soup or just enough so everything retains its separate and delicious flavors and textures. I say drop in a little at a time, it really brings everything together in the most wonderful way. It was warm and delicious! The salted fish was exactly as advertised, spicy as all hell! Dude, these chiles are some demon reincarnate spitting hot fire onto all of your taste buds, at the same time meshing really well with what should be an overly salted piece of fried fish. They come with some tasty sides, a deep fried or soy sauce marinated egg (both hard boiled and equally worth having), and a substantial portion of rice. I found it a bit hellfire for my taste but my girlfriend loved it. The combination pork platter was a trio of swine...sausage slices, pork belly, and roasted pork. The sweet, salty, and savory combinations were on point, and the accompanying pickles, rice, eggs, and chile-potatoes are enough to leave you full and sated to the point of food coma. I would eat this and the mie komplit as a glut-lunch with take home for dinner any day of the week. We ended up ordering a fried chicken entree, another mie komplit, and rice cake curry to go, as well as two delicious homemade cookie desserts...yeah we may have overdone it a bit. All in all, one appetizer, six entrees, and two desserts...grand total of under sixty bucks! All that damn goodness for about 7 bucks a pop! Worth it...stop reading and go already!

I hands down LOVE this place. I eat here weekly, and have been for years. They know me and my family and give us a warm welcome every time. The food is always amazing. The buffet makes it easy to try new things. The chicken tikki marsala is the BEST I've tasted. The mango lassie is to die for. Also try the vegetable samosas. They are the best i have tasted from anywhere in this area. Matter of fact the best EVER. The wait staff is very attentative to your needs. They are excellent. It's very clean in this establishment, and the manager always comes over to make sure your meal is ok. Very humbling, sometimes he'll even serve food which is a plus. They are so good! You must eat here! As of lately, The price for the buffet per person has gone up. I'm guessing due to all the popularity. I remember when it was $12 per person, now it is $15. Considering it is all you can eat, and they offer appetizers, main dishes, and dessert, it still isn't that bad.

If you are looking for something different and casual for dinner, check out this place. The space itself is very cute and welcoming. I thought the staff was wonderful. I got a veggie kabob which was healthy but not very tasty. My boyfriend got the beef kabob and was absolutely in love. Its BYOB and we enjoyed a very nice dinner there on a Friday night, I would definitely go back!

WOW, so impressed with the renovations! In my book, this Remedy location, has gone up at least 3 stars since my last visit. I first stopped into Remedy a few years back and just hated it! It was old, run down and smelt terrible and the customer service was not good. And I know some people liked that "starving student" hang-out vibe... I did not. It was gross. I never came back. (I actually thought I had written a 2 star review - guess not). Then I was asked to meet there for a meeting, so begrudgingly I went. To my surprise the place has completely been re-done. Remedy is now airy, clean and fresh. The gross moldy-pachouli hybrid smell has been replaced with the heavenly smell of delicious foods. And the customer service - well, lets just say I was quite impresses! The young man working the counter went out of his was to be helpful. Even making taster size versions of a chai for us to try out. Remedy Garneau, I will be back. (But not the downtown location, that one's crap wifi irks me to no end!)

I experienced the Jamaican jerk hit the past Sunday for the first time and let me tell you. Amazing! I had the curry chicken which was absolutely delicious. The cabbage was just right and the rice and beans added the perfect flavor. We had the beef patties as an appetizer and they were great. The flakes were to die for. My favorite was the plantain that came with the meal. The best part was that they were on groupon. I love s good deal. The downside was that the restrooms were way in the back but it was no big deal.
Delicious fried rice! Decent service...able to grab a quick dinner before the evening started.

Went here because Ian Freobe (moron) reviewed it in RFT recently (I wanted to take a friend for gyros and now could kick myself for not sticking with St Louis Gyro Company). Anyway, Freobe or whatever that dorks name is, does not mention that the gyro meat has it's own "Special lamb sauce" which is totally unnecessary and totally defeats the purpose of rotating it on a spit in it's own juice. Guess what? The special process means that when they bring the gyro to your table it is ICE FRIGGING COLD!!!!! Totally unacceptable. Totally poor spin. You morons who state this is the best have got to be kidding me. Get back on your meds! The falafel was good, if bland. Where are your sauces (hot/med/mild) to pour on? Anyone who has enjoyed a good street falafel in the middle east would know what I am talking about. Freobe, once again you have proved that you are a jackass. Gyro Express...try microwaving your meat after your special applique'...if I wanted a cold meal I'd go to Ted Drewe's.

This has become our go-to Indian restaurant, despite the fact that we live a block from House of India, possibly the most popular place in town. The main reason is that they have a dinner buffet on Friday and Saturday nights. We've been there a bunch of times for dinner buffet and we enjoy it so much more than ordering from a menu. Their buffet has a huge variety of entrees and sides, definitely more than most Indian buffets have for lunch. We went tonight and the food was exceptional. I don't know if they have a new chef or something, but everything was just fantastic. So why four stars instead of five? The staff there has one habit that drives me crazy - they wipe off clean silverware with a towel in the corner and throw it into a silverware bin. It's so loud that I don't know how anyone can bear to have a conversation while they do that. Also, when they clear dishes from a table, they practically toss them into a buspan, making a huge racket. I know this sounds like a minor gripe, but it happens every time we go and it's a huge annoyance. If the food wasn't so great we'd go somewhere else.

The restaurant is small yet quaint with some Indian decor scattered around. It is one of my favorite Indian restaurants to go to. Their chicken tikka masala is a classic. If this is your first time eating Indian food, I would definitely recommend getting this here. You can never go wrong with chicken. My personal favorite is the Palak lamb. The base is spinach with herbs, onions, tomatoes, ginger, and garlic. Their curry is just so savory with all of the fresh spices and ingredients they use. Im a little surprised that rice doesn't come with the curry and costs extra. Other than that, their naan is also very good especially since it always comes out hot and fresh.
This place insults Chinese cuisine much like Olive Garden does to Italian. I'll shank someone w/ chopsticks if they ever suggested this dump.

I FINALLY got to try Thai 5 after it sat in my bookmarks for far too long. We ordered through Postmates because yes, we are that lazy even though it is right down the street. After reading all the Yelp reviews, we went with the Crab Rangoons, Banana Coins, Drunken Noodles (medium), and Duck Fried Rice (medium). All were amazing!! The Crab Rangoons were delicious and the Sweet Chili Sauce that came with it was surprisingly really good. The Drunken Noodles were very spicy even after asking for it medium, but so full of flavor with lots of fresh vegetables. The Duck Fried rice was topped with crispy fried duck that melted in your mouth. To end the meal, the Banana Coins were the perfect compliment to the spicy Thai food. They're basically fried bananas with honey but they were amazing, I've never had anything like them before. Portion sizes were huge, the two of us definitely could have split one entree. Prices were very reasonable as well. If they offered their own delivery service, this would be my go-to. I'll be back to try the Crab Fried Rice and the Pad Thai!
Best Thai food I have ever had. Great Panang Curry. The spring rolls were good as well.
Delightful experience. We enjoyed a lot the food. The Pad Thai and the coconut soup are my favorite dishes. The banana and chocolate spring rolls are also amazing. Best BYOB in the area.

Meh, the food seems to be a bit off and a little bland. Prices are decent and the vibe just seems weird to me. If you are really craving Vietnamese food and nothing else is open, you might give this a try. It wont kill you but might not satisfy your craving either.

Arrived around 1pm on a Thursday and the place was mostly empty. The lunch buffet was on special, so I paid just over $7 for a filling meal. Not bad. There were several veggie and meat dishes of varying spicy-hotness, so there is certainly something to please all if you go in a group. One thing I really appreciated was that the dishes had different flavor profiles Too often buffets like this play it safe and everything ends up tasting nearly the same. Definitely do NOT go for the decor or ambiance. The place should probably take out the big screen TVs and replace them with mirrors and upgraded wall decor. Side note: Eating the ends of an Indian buffet is not necessarily the smartest thing to do before jumping on an airplane, but I am happy to report no ill side effects.

It's a good spot for lunch when you don't want to wait for a table or service, meaning it's not crowded. Food is good quality and price reflects this. The salmon croissant sandwich is good, could use a little more sauce so the croissant doesn't seem so dry. Beer and wine is good, service is good overall (I never like it when a server says "it's all good here" or worse "gee I've never tried either of those" but overall it was a good experience each of the three times I've had lunch here. My friend has a burger every time he goes here so that says something about the burgers! They put fried egg on their burger, which I understand lots of people like. Not my thing but there are other choices for picky eaters. I've heard their brunch is good but I personally haven't tried it yet. Maybe this weekend?
Excellent food and very good service. My wife and I have the no. 1 meat combo platter. Everything on it was very tasty and had a nice balance. Well seasoned but not overly spicy. Will come back.

If the young girl isn't working, don't eat here! This place was our go to pho place. The soups came out fast, and food was always good. Here's why we won't be back. My husband, son & I went it on a Tuesday, and it wasn't busy. The mom took our order which was 2 soups. We watched two tables who came in after us get our food when we realized it was already 40 minutes and no soups we decided to wait another 5 minutes, but still no soup. We ended up leaving and told them they took to long. There's so many other better pho restaurants around, they need to step it up

Probably in my top 2 favorite places in Brandon... Food is quality, crisp, and super fresh. Great blend of flavors in everything on the menu. I went for a time where I had to have the pad-thai at least once a week. Never really that busy (but they should be). Staff is super friendly and attentive, Price is low if you are looking at the over all picture and compare it to the worth. THIS PLACE IS SUPER CLEAN!!!! Which in my opinion is a good way to judge a quality restaurant.... and this place is spotless. Not kidding at all on this,,, you could literally eat off the floors in the bathroom. Spotless. If you live any where in the Tampa/Brandon area, do yourself a favor and check this place out... I want them to do well because I want to be able to eat there next time I am in town!!!!!!!!!!
Fantastic variety of dishes. If going for gluten free njira order ahead of time. The best way to wrap up the meal is with the Ethiopian coffee.

Hands down the best Indian food in STL. Tried Indian restaurants all over the city, none of them even comes close to the authenticity of the taste that i experienced here. Each and every item on the buffet was outstanding, which makes it even more extraordinary considering buffet items general are bland and tasteless. Keep up the outstanding establishment, hope to come here more often
This is one of my go-to restaurants in Carpinteria. Siam Elephant has great service, a lovely patio, and consistently delicious food.

Came here because I was dying for a bahn mi, I got a pretty basic sandwich with no sauce on it, the veggies weren't pickled, and the meat was a joke. I also got service with attitude and the bare minimum interaction. Guess my search for a good bahn mi goes on.
Excellent food, attentive service, big portions. A MUST TRY RESTAURANT IN EDMONTON!!

Love, Love, Love this place! I last ate their a few months ago. The decor is simple, but the food TOTALLY makes up for it. So far it's my favorite place. The wine list is not extensive, but they have good choices and decent prices. The food is very inexpensive for what you get. The food is soooo good! I love their mango chicken dish. They have a lunch and dinner menu. For lunch you can get a great meal for under $10. The wait staff we have every time have been very nice. Oh, my favorite part.... ask for their hot sauce (Masoula - sp?). It's awesome if you like hot stuff. Just ask for the hot sauce! Try it.... you won't regret it! They also have a sangria that's yummy. On a hot day, it's quite refreshing.
We just ate at the Persian room and I must say the food was wonderful. The inside of the restaurant was so beautiful the service was great. Dinner was a little expense but while worth it.

First, the good. We ate outside which was nice. The food we ordered was very good. The bad. You are given a tiny menu with food that states its to share and prices for sharing. We ordered the special which was a dinner (THERE ARE NO DINNER PRICES ON THE MENU) and there is a reason for this. I had sea bass to the tune of $38 my date had Veal $42. The portions were very small. We are not big people. Do not go here if you are hungry or on a budget. This restaurant is way, way, over priced. You can do alot better elsewhere. My biggest complaint though is they are not forthcoming with the prices. If you order dinner you better ask what it will cost or risk heart failure when you get the bill.

My friends and I wandered into Samson Kabob House not knowing what to expect. Wow! Am I glad we did. The restaurant is beautiful, the service excellent and the food was out of this world. We had several vegetarian dishes and found them to be outstanding. I highly recommend the following appetizers: kadu (pumpkin), burani (eggplant) and ashak (dumplings). There were leftovers and I enjoyed them the next day just as much. This is my new favorite restaurant in the area.

Friends in Phoenix told us in San Diego that this place in Tucson was worth the drive. We were in Tucson for New Years so we made it a point to stop in. It did not disappoint. The lunch buffet had deliciously seasoned choices that were better than many meals we had in India. Many classic dishes. A continuous supply of fresh nan. This will be a regular stop any time we get near Tucson.

Went with my wife and daughter on a Groupon. The room was fairly empty when we arrived but by the time we left it was completely full. Nice to see this restaurant succeed--and it succeeds on the merits of the food. We ordered four main courses, and the flavors were completely varies from dish to dish. All were fully seasoned and nicely spicy, as we requested. The Indian food just blows Tiffan out of the water. We also had Hakka noodles which were excellent. There was a lot of food to take home, so I look forward to eating it again. We will definitely be returning.
Really good fried chicken and mac & cheese. Also a fan of the biscuits. Can't eat it too often because it's so unhealthy, but like it when I do. Only issue is that it's a bit expensive.

It's a good thing they are at a great location with a great view because the service is terrible and the food is just ok. The first time I went, I sat in the corner of the bar to get a view of the sunset. There was definitely drama going on between the bartenders and the wait staff. The bartenders openly complained to me about individual wait staff and continued to talk poorly about them behind their backs. The second time I went, the bartender served one beer and asked me to close out because it was the end of her shift even though I was running a tab. She also asked a couple the same thing as they ordered their meal. The third time, I called ahead to check hours on Christmas Eve. The person on the phone said they were closing at 6. I got there at 4 and was only told, "we are closing now. You got some bad information." No apology, just a rude tone. They do have cheap beers and a beautiful sunset view. I keep going back for these, hoping the service will get better. So far, it hasn't...

I'm a Newtown local, but have never before Sunday night "eaten in" at Guru's - we've always ordered home and had it delivered or picked it up. An unexpected visitor was the occasion for us to see Priya, and the experience was a very nice one. She was very happy to have us as personal guests instead of the usual routine of ordering over-the-phone and a resulting quick chit-chat at pick-up time. Arriving at 5PM (opening time) with the place not yet populated allowed us to have a more substantial dialogue with Priya. She introduced us to our very earnest waiter, a young guy who seemed to be very happy to have us there in general, but was even happier to tell us about all the dishes he felt we should try since he liked them so much! Rita (my wife) ordered a vegetarian dish, our guest selected some Tandoori, and I opted for Lamb Vindaloo, prepared "Indian hot". The main courses and the samosa/breads that we also chose were all quite good (tastier than our take-out experiences, since we were able to have the food almost immediately as opposed to somewhat cooled after a short drive home). While I'm no "expert" on Indian cuisine, in my earlier years I spent nearly a half-year total working in various Indian cities, where I sampled all sorts of different regional Indian foods, and Guru's is exceptional, Also, as prior Northern-NJ-ites before residing in PA, we've also had many meals in the "India" of NJ, the Metuchen/Edison area (with friends of families of some of those restaurants) - and Guru's favorably compares to nearly all of them. Visit some time soon and you'll be pleased with the food AND the hospitality.

Two words, FALAFEL BUFFET. I know that also sounds like thunder thighs buffet, but hey, some buffets you just have to try. Every Saturday there's an Iranian/Mediteranian buffet. Falafel, Kabob, sometimes curry, Its awesome. During weekdays the food is always cooked and seasoned wonderfully and its a great experience every time. This family owned restaurant is such a good addition to our community. Its hard to find a restaurant where you have contact with the owners in every experience. This place measures up as they have several times made special orders for me and comped delicious soups and appetizers. Its a must try for all Reno-ites.

A friend recommended this place to me yesterday and I just had to check it out today. It's a little hole in the wall in a small plaza. They serve hot food that is ready for easy order and pickup but they also have a menu which you order and wait for and either eat in or take out. Keep in mind if you plan on eating in that it is a small place. 1 merengue (drink), 1 chicken empanadilla, 1 plate of mofongo with shrimp, black beans and white rice -- all for $16.15 (after tax)
Food is delicious and a great value! I wish it was closer so I could get dinner from here too!

Service was alright, ambience was ok. I felt like it was kind of dead for it being around dinner time. My husband had the teriyaki chicken with rice but it was pretty salty. My sushi was great though so I can't complain. Probably wouldn't go back there if I was in the area.

A new place that we just discovered! Great food and very reasonable place. I enjoyed their service and food. I love their Thai tea! Also, I like their dishes because they don't use excess salt. Definately recommend this place.

The chawla kadu is amazing! The food here is great and you can't beat the prices. Don't let the exterior fool you. It's a very clean,nice restaurant. The service can be a bit slow but it is worth it! Don't forget your wine because it is a BYOB.
Good food but the buffet does not offer varieties like other indian restaurants!!!

I let the owner know that this was my first time trying Thai food, and tried a dish under her recommendation. It had red curry which I didn't like very much. The first few bites were ok but I couldn't go further than that. When she came back I told her I didn't care for the dish and her reply was "next time you can try something else" I was really disappointed she didn't offer for me to try something else. I was going to try the Thai Pad before she suggested this other dish. SIDE NOTE : The sushi was delish. Glad I ordered it otherwise I would have gone to bed hungry.

Stop #4 on the NOLA food + cocktail tour... me thinks we should've quit while we were ahead. We were lucky to grab two seats at the bar on a Saturday night. My "Wry Smile" cocktail was fine (rye, rhubarb, grand poppy, sherry), but my gf's "Louisville Slugger" was too smoky my taste. I was thinking "smoked vanilla" would be smoky-toasty, but it was smoky-scotchy. Not for me. We ordered the stracciatella, one of my fave cheeses, which came with roasted squash and hazelnuts. Unfortunately, the nuts had a rancid flavor that ruined the dish. The server was totally cool about it, took it away and didn't charge us even though we had already taken more than a few bites. IDK, maybe it's just me since the place was busy, but not a place I'd go back to.

I had probably the best sandwich ever here, but the customer service leaves something to be desired. The two gentlemen behind the counter were accommodating and courteous but the lady at the register was crude, offensive, and beyond unprofessional.
